I've been over that story since I was十七. No thank you, I'd rather babysit our nephew all night than be stuck on a barstool pretending to care about some bloke saying he remembers my face.      Oh, hush. He was so swoon-worthy, remember? And don’t forget, he brought us those pastries to make up for it. Didn’t even want to charge us. You paid anyway like you always do. Still, I’m with you, no need to go back. Our nephew is like a squishier, sleepier version of our niece’s dog. Ten minutes of him and I’m home with a pick and I’m out the door. Living my best life.      Yeah, he really is the cutest. Reminds me so much of my first born. I remember that, you were out working the night I went into labour, and I had to text you like,  “Here I am, the doctor says if we land a baby in the water we only live once.”  You just called me back and laughed, and then said, “Hang on love, I just Baptised a new client.”       Laughs  “You weren’t supposed to take that as serious as you did. I was already in the car by the time they said 'He’s on the way'. Honestly, you were my rock the whole time. I can’t remember what you had for dinner either night, you worked and came through. That’s all I remember. You’re my most reliable person. I’m lucky to have you.      Aww, stop it. You’re not bad yourself. I know you've not been working as much these past months. My sister, for heaven’s sake, you’re allowed to slow down. The rest of us suffer the day you retire. What are we supposed to do without your witty scheming?       Smiles  Well, I'm thinking of trying the lunches with a new friend from my old wedding do. She’s got a veg box delivery idea with a twist—local, seasonal, go-to-home gourmet stuff. I’ve been testing some recipes at home.      Oh, fantastic. You’ve got the eye for what your people want. So, have you made it to her place yet?

So did you manage to sort out your paperwork for the six-month stay in Spain? I remember they tightened up all those travel rules after Brexit.      I did, thank God. It took a little while—applied for the UK Global Heath Insurance card and the European Health Insurance Card for my mum. Felt like I was going through airport security all over again every time I presented them at the border. Did you take your EHIC last summer when you were in France?      I did, yeah. Know what's funny? The first time I arrived in Marseille, the man at the border just winked at me and said  “Still no queues, is there?”  Like he was commenting on how well the post-Brexit system was working! I nearly bit his head off, to be honest.      I think he probably meant it kindly, in that French way. How was it when you moved from town to town in Italy with your mates in 2020? I remember you told me you showed up at a hostel in Naples with just your EHIC and one sandwich.      Oh yeah! I mean, we were a bit overconfident, thinking we’d deal with anything on the way. But the bus got stuck in Bari for hours. I remember – Mateo borrowed his mum’s €50 because he thought his debit card wouldn’t work in Italy anymore and it  did , obviously. Still, we didn’t regret it. That’s the beauty of just going with it, right?      Definitely. I oddly miss the ease of flitting from country to country without overthinking. But now I feel like I  have  to plan because it’s about paperwork as much as travel. I’m just trying to remember to keep my passport valid for  at least  six months beyond any trip now. It’s not unmanageable, just… less spontaneous.      True. Though I will say, once you’re in a country it feels just as free as it did before. I met this guy in Lisbon who told me about how he used to travel on Eurostar with just a phone printout of his EHIC from his phone. Now he says he scans it and sends it to his travel mates beforehand so they can check go through faster on his own if he’s late.      That’s a clever idea. I’d go mad trying to keep everything in one place.

Right, who wants jelly and cream for dessert? Or would you prefer something else?      Jelly and cream! And can we have biscuits as well?      Me too! I want the £200 one from the Monopoly box, like the big one.      Oh no, not the 'Big Mr Monopoly' again! You two have been playing that board game for  hours . I swear, every time we watch a programme, it’s Monopoly.      Because it's fun! And we get to say things like "Go directly to jail!"      Yeah, and the bit where you can steal money from other people is the best. I’ve already got so much I can’t count it anymore.      I’m sad to say the only thing I’m counting now is the number of times I’ve heard “Do you need to buy that house or not?!”      Mummy, can we move to Park Lane? It’s the fanciest!      Yeah! And then we can get three houses and a hotel!      For goodness’ sake, just move… although, if we’re talking about moving, maybe we should consider selling some properties. This game is making me consider actually buying a bigger house.      Mummy, what’s the point of the “Free Parking” square? Nothing happens!      That’s what I’ve been asking myself for years, love.      Also, can Daddy have marshmallows and custard for dessert?  He  said it would be “cool” even though he knows the rest of us hate the mess.      No, not this time. Marshmallows are only if it’s  his  go. My house, my rules.      I want custard and jelly too.      Do we have to share the Monopoly money when we’re done?      Only if you want to keep playing with your pockets full of paper money! Now go and grab your plates, you two, and come back in one piece. That game can go from friendly to brutal in about three turns.      Is it almost bedtime yet?      If you finish your custard and jelly, then maybe. But if you keep arguing over whether you landed on “Chance” or not, I'll say it's midnight and you're out.      I’m not arguing! I  did  land on "Chance"!      Then lucky you. Now go get the desserts, and try not to trade me your house for a scribbled note from the Free Parking square. Not again. So do you not find it a bit weird that they gave us a tax code for the first time in like...ever and I don’t even have a job yet?      What do you mean? You applied for that grant or whatever, and the HMRC picked it up through Universal Credit or whatever it’s called now, yeah?      Yeah, but I’m literally self-employed on a paper—a transcription job I once did in uni! I never even invoiced anyone. It was just a one-off. But now they’re like, “Here’s your tax code.” Like,  why?       Lakelands? That was the short-term thing, right? You know, like that MyUniTranscribe gig? I swear my cousin’s lawyer tried to do the same thing once and got chased around by the IFRS people for months. It’s like they’ve got software better than quantum computing tracking every single thing you touch. Even the stuff in your browser cache, you ever looked?      I did—and I still don’t understand why that solicitor would do that, but maybe he was just trying to write it off or something.      It’s not even as simple as that anymore—it’s machine learning. The government doesn’t just “think” you’ve earned something: it  knows  you’ve earned it because some algorithm flagged a Word document in your cloud drive and compared it to a contract. And now you’re on the record.      Oh no. I’m not filing my tax return already, am I?      Pretty much. It’s like you’re being categorised under passive income or something. You know, most people about your age don’t even have to do the thing now. It’s all automated. The only ones who get issued actual tax codes like you are the ones who managed to be both inactive and accidental.      So what’s the next step? Am I supposed to open a limited company or something? ‘Cause I don’t feel like I’m a business yet. I still shop at budget stores and I use filters to make myself look like a proper person sometimes.      Some people do. The irony is, the more passive it is—which the system thinks it is—the more it wants you to act like a proper business. But if you do that, they see it as a reaction, and then it’s like your hobby officially became a career.

Rather do this than watch the telly all night, ain't I?      Oh aye, I’ll take a cup of that, love. Not had a proper chat in ages.      Yes, the telly’s all very well, but it don’t give half the fun as a nice cup of tea and a good old chinwag.      I remember when I worked on the old canal project back in ’72. Built a new lock system right under the city. Thought I’d.Fatalfanstay outside when it rained. Mud up to my neck, but it was grand.      Oh, I’d have dropped dead in that lot. Me, I preferred my time fixing roofs and putting on tiles. Probably why I’ve still got the back, eh? I’ll be the first up if the roof lets water in.      And then I’d be the one making the tea while you two were out fixing it! No, you didn’t spare a thought for the poor ones like me, did you?      Nonsense, Mabel! You did your bit as well. Did you think for a minute I’d’ve got through three kids without you?      Oh, pish! I looked after more than three in me time, Harold!      It’s true, what she says. If I’d ‘ad you at the weekend, I wouldn’t’ve got past Sunday afternoon. Strictly tea at half past ten, and then I had a choice—more tea or out with a broom.      That’s because you couldn’t make a sandwich about five days a week!      Well, I had to be a bit clever about it, seeing as I didn’t have the handle.      My, my! You lot certainly weren’t afraid to make a point. Me and the lads, it was a different story. We relied on someone to bring us sandwiches when we were out on the site. Those lads could’t cut a sandwich to save their lunches.      Now, love, no need for that. You come home and I’d have dinner waiting. Stew or something hearty. I’d say “sit down and stop loosening your legs, you old donkey,” but you’d be too proud to listen.      I’ll admit it, though, after twenty years of working, I had to stop. My legs gave in like a sheet over a bed. Cursed them every day I wasn’t workin’.      Aye, I know the feeling. You see me trying to do the crossword and my fingers won’t want to write straight.

So did you get the labels printed?      Aye, just today, they came first thing in the post. I had to order more ink for my printer before I could stick ‘em on the jars.      That’s brilliant! Have you sorted the website out yet? Got a photo gallery or something?      I’ve got the site up—still not looking a million dollars, though. I borrowed a friend’s camera to take some pictures but the lighting was all over the place. You’d have to teach me how to take decent product shots or something.      I’d be happy to! I’ve done a bit of photography for supply companies when working on training materials. My student discounts helped me get a basic lighting kit. It makes a massive difference.      That’d be great. I’ve been trying to make everything sound eco-friendly and ‘clean’ when I post online. I’ve been re-using jars and only using natural preservatives. People seem to like that, even if they’re not using the products yet.      That’s the way to go. These days, people look for authenticity. You’re bound to build a loyal base, especially with your story—your gran used to make her own stuff, right?      Mate, I got the recipe from her old journal, written in the back of a Brownie sash, mind you. Silly old cow. But yeah, I keep mentioning her in the 'About' section. It’s a bit emotional but it adds a bit of personality.      Exactly! And it adds a unique angle. Any word from the social media influencer you spoke to? The one about doing a collab?      She said she’d get back to me. Maybe next week. Honestly, I’m barely sleeping worrying about it all. Maybe I should do something less ‘cosy’ like drop guest spots in big beauty stores. My cousin’s into that sort of thing—he mentioned a shop in the city centre that stocks local stuff.      That sounds like a good middle ground. Websites and social media take time to develop, but having your product in a physical store gives people a proper chance to try it.      Yeah, that’d be brilliant. I’ve been measuring sample jars and trying to get the right specs for shipping. It’s the box dimensions that get me—tiny jar, big packaging. I’ve made it 30p more in postage than it should be.

Rather annoying isn’t it, this weather.      It's dreadful, I know. I got soaked on my way home from the school run this morning. Poor Jane was soaked as well, she hasn’t got over the sniffles from Tuesday.      Oh darlin’, I saw her at the store last week with you, she looked absolutely fine.      She’s been off with this terrible tummy bug all week, so we had to close the classroom a bit early. We’ve been behind with the curriculum. Didn’t help that the kids had a right grumble about the lack of tests!      Tests at this age? That’s a shock to them.      Oh, they’re primed for them, to be honest. D’you know, I think the head teacher’s even thinking of moving to a more project-based system.      Well, with all the talk these days about mental health and not pressuring kids, maybe it’s time. I used to give them so many exams when I taught, and I always felt awful about it. I mean, don’t get me wrong, tests are fine for assessment, but we’ve got to be kind too.      You’re so right – and it’s not just about curriculum these days, is it?      What do you mean?      Well, you heard about the row in the news this week about the policies for pensions. They say they’re going to change them again. I dread what that’ll mean for retired teachers. You worked in it for thirty years – all that dedication, and now we might have about half of what we expected.      Oh Jane, I didn’t hear that. That’s despicable. We barely have savings as it is, and now to have that taken away from us?      I know. The only surprising thing is the minimal outrage – it was all over the news, but there’s just not the sort of protests or protests we used to get over these things.      I think people are just so exhausted, love. My knees tell me I’m 90 every morning, and I can go out and get a cup of tea or meet up with my bingo mates, but not everyone can do that.      Aye, some of us still have bills to pay and uniforms to iron and roles to fill.      It’s a right laugh, isn’t it? You’re the only one of us still at work.

So did you manage to sort out the central heating yet, Tom? I know it's been freezing in that flat of yours.      It's still on the fritz, to be honest. Got a new thermostat fitted last week, but I think the pipe somewhere is leaking again. I’ve had three different engineers out, and they’re all twitchy about saying what it actually is.      That sounds like a nightmare. Christmas in a chilled-out flat is not ideal, especially if you're supposed to be hosting.      Oh I’m not, don’t worry. My sister’s the poor soul who’s doing the hosting this year. All I’m contributing is the Christmas pudding, and that’s mostly turkey and breadcrumbs by now.      Aye well, I hear you. Danged heating systems and danged modern world! But if you're stuck with the cold, better make breakfast, no? Baked beans in front of a fire in a jumper and socks, the Welsh way!      Haha, typical Dylan. I still can’t get over how much you get done in your shop—woodworking in short sleeves even when it’s minus ten outside. How on earth do you do it?      Call it a Celtic fire in the belly, my dear. Plus, I’ve got a gas heater on the bench. Can’t let all those applewood and ash go to waste.      Speaking of wood, I planted two mulberry trees at the weekend. Honestly, I thought they’d never root, but they’re already got new leaves. Small joys.      Mulberries? That’s wild! We had a mulberry at my mum’s house years ago. My brother bled red juice all over his shirt trying to stuff one into his mouth. Parents were not impressed.      Mulberries are kind of tricky, though. You need to keep them well-pruned or they’ll branch everywhere. Still, the fruit is a joy when you can get it.      Aye, nothing like picking fruit and then hoisting it up a ladder to make jam. Or a new whiskey barrel if I’m feeling fancy.      You're living the life, Dylan. I still live on toast and Thai takeaway.      Same here really. Just swap the Thai for curry in a tin and chips from the freezer aisle.      I seriously envy your freedom though, Tom. As a researcher, I’m tied to this institution like a cactus glued to a brick.

Rather annoying isn't it.      What’s the matter?      Our cutlery drawer is officially full. We don’t have a single clean fork left at home. I’m starting to feel like we have to bring our own silverware like in a takeaway.      I understand the problem very well. I reckon it’s not as bad as most people think. A lot of people would love to have a problem like that.      That’s true. It’s just that the last time I washed up, I thought I’d done the lot, but obviously, I haven’t because I still found a wet fork in the sink this morning.      I’m living with an eccentric left-hander. Ten spoon, one fork, and two knives, and somehow I’m expected to find a piece of cutlery that doesn’t have something breakfast-y on it. It’s a continuous problem.      And the oversized knife hides, you know, it's so thick. Good for cutting through steak like you would do here, but for something like a salad or occasional falafel, it’s like using a bulldozer on a butterfly.      You'd think in a house this big we'd at least have one drawer with fairly organized stuff in it.      Yeah, but don’t you know what the solution is? I always blame the young generation for not washing up properly, but someone at some point has also got to not read the manual. Those forks are not going to clean themselves. Also, some people shouldn’t be allowed near tea kettles, but that's a different story.      I think you’re wrong. I’m very careful. I just don’t have the time or energy to do it every day. I’m doing a decent chunk to do most of it over the weekend.      Mm hmm. I do a bit of it on the weekend as well.      You mustn’t expect too much from either of them. They’ve only just left their parents recently, right? They're probably waiting for their silverware to do it all by itself.      Yeah, go on then. But it's not like there are so many of us in the house, is there? It's just three of us.      So why have we made it so hard to manage one drawer full of basic silverware?      I expect it’s the fact that this is the sort of house that collected cutlery like they were vintage toasters or knives that collect dust.

Right love, just wanted to go through our plans for the ski trip again before Sunday. I’ve been thinking... What d'ya reckon about flying into Geneva instead of Grenoble this time?      Mmm. Why?      Well, I saw a few places in Chamonix that looked nice and the drive from the airport is shorter than driving up all them winding roads into the French Alps from Grenoble.      Is easier?      Yeah, and we might be able to check into the lodge a bit earlier. Still under the same budget too, as long as we book the train tickets flexible enough.      Yeah, like that MyFavio one we did last time? The one with the lake view?      Exactly. I think it’s still available if we move up a day. Got a bit breakfast, by the way? I’m starving.      Yes, the toast! . Also, the skiing, is it that man-made one or the big slopes?      A mix, honestly. Want to go early morning when it's less crowded, but also want to do the proper ones where it feels like we’re really out there – y'know, the real slopes and stuff.      Yeah! And don’t forget to check the phone’s memory – I already filmed you at your desk, and the coffee was someone else in the background again.      Oh for god’s sake – what was that, the third meeting in three days and still no client sign-off? I swear, it’s like trying to get water from a stone!      Well, at least you didn’t wear your blue socks yesterday.      Don’t wanna talk about my socks. My day was long enough.      Sorry Mummy. But I do like the green gloves you mentioned on the video call. You looked posh.      Feels posh. Though being asked to summarise a 47-page report in five minutes was anything but.      You’re so good at that.      I bloody well had to be. Any road, I made a dent in the slides, so maybe we can box this up on Friday.      Yippee! So we can focus on skiing next week?      True to that. I’ll start packing over the weekend. Cram them waterproofs in a suitcase... You up for going for a walk this weekend? Might clear the head after the week I’ve had.      Yeah, want to see the birds by the stream?      Course you do. Just don’t mention the green gloves again.      Shhhh!

So did you actually do your maths homework last night or just pretend you did it again?      What, and bore myself to death? I watched  Money Heist  instead. It’s not like we were revising proper anyway. Miss said half of it was just copying the questions from the board and then answering them  exactly  as they were. I reckon it wasn’t actually… real learning. Like, I mean, if I’m doing this stuff again next week, it’ll just be easier to copy it off the internet or sommat. You know how it is, don’t you?      Ugh yeah,  Money Heist  is good but maths is still annoying. I managed like three questions before I got distracted by my Spotify. I put on this playlist that I made called “Songs to Cry to While Doing Algebra”.      Oh no, what’s on it?       Midnight Memories  by Halsey, and that new Billie Eilish song, and some James Arthur. Real sad bops, basically. I was sobbing into my textbook by the end of it. I mean, seriously, who designed the exam paper and decided that  simultaneous equations  should be named that? That’s a mental health crisis waiting to happen.      I agree, like, it just  sounds  dramatic. I reckon the teacher thought that would scare us into trying harder. But no, it just made me want to fake an illness. So what about Spanish homework? That stuff is a nightmare, right?      Yeah, the past tense verbs and all the irregular ones. Can you even  spell  the past tense of “to make” without Googling it? I spent 20 minutes just trying to write what my mum said yesterday in Spanish and then I gave up and just said  “Hablé de paz”  like I’m some lone wolf expressing my inner thoughts.      Oh god, was that all in the subjunctive tense too?      Of course it was. I just panicked. I ended up trying to draw a timeline on the back of the paper with the tenses written in  stick figures . You know like that guy from the history gothic movie who time-travels or something?      Yeah, the one that wears a cloak and lives in the shadows.      Exactly! So I made it to the past perfect one and then my mind just shut down. But anyway, what’s next week in Food Tech? I asked my sister and she said something about making homemade mac ‘n’ cheese.

Rather skip the new films in the cinema love to get grumpy. I know it's supposed to be exciting with all the big names and giant heroes, but honestly, I prefer a good old classic where you know who is going to win.      Grandmum, you haven’t even seen half of the new releases yet. Some of them actually have quite a clever story behind all the explosions and CGI. I think you’d like one called  The Last Guardian  – it’s more of a historical action film with a moral twist.      Oh yes, I remember  The Last Guardian , like, very old film! Not the new one, the 1970s one with that lovely actors what’s his name – Stewart something. Terry Stewart. It was about a young man sent back in time, and he was the only one who could stop the bad guys, but the twist is he had to give up everything he loved to do it. Hugely moving.      No, Grandmum, that was  The Time Traveler’s Wife . The one I’m talking about is completely different. Though I have to say, your memory for films is incredible. It’s something I still try to learn from watching how you describe things without getting confused.      Well it's mostly because I didn’t grow up with all these new film styles and names. It was just reels and a programme on the side. You didn’t need fancy sets, just a good story.      That’s what a lot of people are starting to appreciate again – something real, something with meaning. Not all these superhero sagas – I get it, it’s fun, but I miss films that made us think about our lives.      Exactly! Like  Educating Rita  that was a film I really liked. It was about this working-class woman, like me, who wanted to get her head into books and learning. And the man who taught her – a scholar stuck in his own world, but she changed him. I cried at the end, such a beautiful ending.      Oh I remember  Educating Rita ! I took an English class on it once, it's so good. I think watching films can go hand in hand with life if you let it.      Oh, I see you're always the clever one. You went to your university and you learned all that about films and literature. I just sat in the cinema hours after work with cup of tea and a programme on the armrest and watched whatever was on.

So did you talk to him yet about the whole thing with the garden gate?      No, and I don’t even want to start yet. I’ve had enough with the council trying to fine me because my “cut grass height” is “questionable.” Imagine. Ten pounds for my grass being two inches too  alive .      Oh come on, that’s not fair. You’ve only had your cat’s ashes in the garden since January. You can’t be expected to dump her in a river and call it a day.      That’s what the squirrel says, but I guess authority does  not  like cats with posthumous residential rights.      Anyway, enough about that. So what are you doing this weekend? I’m thinking I’ll finally tackle the bookshelf I bought off the kerb. It’s got about 20 years of breakfast on it and God knows what else.      Blooming hell. I remember that bookshelf. It’s the one that had a  nest  in it when I pushed it, didn’t it?      Oh no! I didn’t notice that when I got it. I’ve got a parrot now, by the way. His name is Tony.      Tony? Why Tony?      Because he keeps saying “Tony,” and I thought,  right, well if you’re going to name me, I might as well make the most of it .      Sounds like a madhouse. I’m just resting up for my Saturday morning gin and being grumpy at the park with your dad. He’s entered a pétanque tournament now.      Oh for heaven’s sake — what’s next, he going to learn to rhoomba and handle it like a superhero sidekick?      If he keeps this up, he’ll start charging people to watch him win.      So have you tried using that app your friend gave you? The one for managing your court schedule and things?      I downloaded it, then the phone took over. I think it’s a foreign government trying to capture my life points by now.      It’s not that hard. Let me come over on Sunday and show you. I’ll teach you how to use it — and maybe you could help me clean the bookshelf? We could charge it to the hours of madness regenerated.      Sounds like a deal. Just make sure Tony isn’t sitting near the bucket. I’ve been accused of throwing cat custard.      And to think I only brought you coffee for this.

Rather skip the queue and just go through the side doors, do you reckon?      I suppose, if they're open. Otherwise, we’ll end up waiting an hour again.      Not to mention they have those dodgy automatic ones at the centre entrance — my phone accidentally flashed the gate open last week while I was拍照 [taking photos].      I remember that — it was halfway through your lecture too, wasn’t it?      Yes! And one of the students behind me thought it was part of the teaching method. Told me I was very futuristic.      That’s your department, isn’t it? "If they don’t smile, you change the slides."      Probably, yeah. I’m starting to feel like I should hand out hazard pay. Or an aspirin at the very least.      I’ve been thinking about that — in my lecture today, I had to stop mid-flow because the projector picked up the glare from my glasses. One bloke nearly walked out, he was so confused.      Oh no! What did you say to him?      Just told him I was demonstrating how important it is to paraphrase. Made the most awkward laugh, but I think it worked.      You’re a legend. You know, you should record one of your lectures and call it  The Lost Art of Panic Hilarious Spontaneity .      That’s oddly endearing. Some students still don’t know what a semicolon is, though. Can you believe it?      I did a grammar walk-through the other day, and one of them asked if Latin and Greek were still considered “okay” to learn. I said only if you want to be both confused and impressive at dinner parties.      That’s about right. I’m actually planning a minimal shopping trip tomorrow afternoon. We need toothpaste, and I miss having decent English biscuits.      You mean  proper  biscuits, with layers and a little bit of digestive in there?      Exactly. I’ve tried these local ones, and they go straight from crisp to mud if you even  look  at them wrong.      Don’t even remind me — I bought what I thought was chocolate digestives, and I seriously questioned my life choices for about two hours.      True story. But we can’t get over this, we’ve got lectures to give tomorrow. Suck it up and pretend we’re Channel Islanders.      And always carry a toothpick, in case.      Exactly. Now, let’s try to avoid the long line of students arguing about whether Postmodernism is dead for the fifth time this week.

Right, so the plan is we're going to the post office first thing, just to drop off that birthday present for Mrs. Thompson she gave us the week before last. Then, I've got a bit of time to pop into the hairdresser before I pick up the kids.      Mummy, is my hair going to look like an alien again this time?      No, you’ve only had your hair cut once! I said I’m not going to turn you into a triangle like last time! This time it's just a little trim, just to get the split ends.      Can I go too?      No, not today, Benjamin. You’ve got your haircut on Thursday. I’m not taking both of you at the same time, I’d never live it down if one of you ran off and hid in the back of the shop again!      He didn’t run off! He just wanted to look at the cakes.      He didn’t want the cakes, he wanted to eat the cakes—right in front of the woman who owns it!      Well, let’s focus on today and not rehash old arguments. After the hairdresser, I’m going to do a bit of shopping. We need milk, bread, and I want to pick up some fresh veg for dinner. Then, I’ll come back here and you’ll be with Aunty Rosie for the afternoon. She’s coming in at ten forty-five.      Aunty Rosie said we can read a dinosaur book and bake cookies!      Yes, she did! And she  might  let us make a cake about five minutes before your dad gets back. But it has to be a quick one. I’ve already warned her—you know that she can barely cook toast without burning it.      Mummy, can I wear my yellow wellies to the photoshoot?      No, Geli. The photoshoot is with the farm, you’ll be taking pictures of the animals, so you  have  to wear clothes you don’t mind getting a bit muddy. But your mismatched socks are going in the bag—just in case.      Can Geli go in the enclosure with the ducks?      No, Benjamin. Geli, no duck cuddles. The box says “educational experience,” not “farm petting zoo.” The ducks might bite, and I won’t have you with broken fingers and bellyache on your dad’s lap in the car.      Mummy, I’m not  that  clumsy!

Okay, I swear this sandwich is 90 per cent mayonnaise and 10 per cent  what used to be chicken . Have you tried today’s lunch option?      Oh yeah, I went for the chicken Caesar wrap… and it tasted like a Caesar  mural  in a dodgy art gallery. I mean, I’ve had better on the 12-step self-help recovery plan.      Honestly, this place is a vibe. One day they’re going to dump someone in the deep fryer and I’m like “Wait, when did the menu include vegan zombies?”      I’m still not over last week when the “saag paneer” tasted like boiling Mycin and bitterness. I’m like, left my home country just to come to this?      Don’t get me started! But hey, if it’s free and you’re not breakfast, no one’s judging. Like, I once survived on just crisps, blackcurrant squash, and daydreams of Marks and Spencer. Good times.      At least you get the crisps properly salted. I once had a bag that tasted like someone tried to make them with tap water from outside… plus municipal sweat.      Holy hell. How are we even surviving uni with this food? I swear it’s a cover up. One day they’re gonna tell us they’re all Silly String and the trays are just for performance art.      Honestly, I think the canteen conspiracy is a real thing. I had a dream— a very real dream —that I opened a “vegetarian pie” and it was a fully functioning calculator made out of mashed potatoes. I woke up crying from the trauma.      I’ve seen things too. One time I thought I saw the custard cream  smirking  at me. And then I left it alone. I passed up dessert. For the first time ever. I was a grown woman, I had standards.      I sort of stick to my “never eat yellow after lunch” rule now. Unless it’s lemonade and it’s been shaken by someone hot. That's a  different  category.      Yeah, go me. I tried it once and ended up yellow for two days and my denture guy came out to do improv on my front steps.      Look, at the end of the day, this canteen is where we bond, right? Like, this is more than just sandwiches and despair over cold chicken. We came here to connect… and to keep my mum from asking why I haven’t put on weight.

So did you lot actually manage to get anything to eat in that supermarket the other day or did they just sell you all the weird organic stuff again?      Honestly, I've given up trying to find anything that isn’t gluten-free or vegan these days—half the stuff doesn’t even make sense. I saw a packet of pasta that said “sun-dried” and “unprocessed”… like, it’s pasta, not a vitamin pill.      No, but I get what they’re doing. If supermarkets don’t cater to the modern demand for clean eating, or whatever it's called now, they’ll go out of business. People want options, even if the labels are just another form of advertising.      Oh, you lot talk like you’ve tried the food, not just the labels. I’m more of a "if it tastes like food and doesn’t make me feel like I’ve breakfasted on a gym supplement, it’s good enough for me" kind of person.      Fair play, I say the same. One time I tried that "vitality range"—personally I think they just dipped it in kale essence.      And then you wonder why we’ve got digestive issues. I swear by rhythm and routine. That and good food at the right time of day. I was in Cornwall last month—best thing was the local fish and chip shop, honestly. Tried their famed "superfood fish and crumpet," which was just battered haddock and full fat custard. Heaven.      That’s so me. I’m still waiting to find a holiday where I don’t spend at least half the time talking about food or watching it on TV. I’m watching a fly-on-the-wall documentary of a restaurant this week. It’s wild how much pressure chefs are under.      Yeah, but it's kind of impressive, isn’t it? The stress, the high standards, all for people just wanting a decent meal. Last time I was on holiday, I fell in love with a little place in Barcelona. Not fancy, but the paella was out of this world.      So what are the plans? We going back there for a bit of a break or just eating the same old takeaway goop?      Honestly, I was thinking of camping somewhere off-grid, no shops, no TV—just food that we make ourselves. No dodgy labels or sustainability marketing.      Sounds like my kind of holiday, as long as there's a supply of coffee and biscuits.

Rather skip the newfit and go to London to see me.      Ah, that’d be lovely, dear. I’ve not seen your place since before all this redevelopment. It’ll be like it was.      Well, it ain't like it was, but it’s still got that old London charm. I was telling   Frank   about it the other day.      I bet he’d have a few opinions on it. You know how he is about architecture.      Oh yes, he’s always moaning about how things get modernised too fast.      Well, Frank’s the only one still around who remembers the old ways.      The new buildings are alright, just not what London was like in the good old days. I remember walking the streets of Bethnal Green, you’ve got to have been there, Doris.      I spent a summer there, planting the Queen’s garden, you know, for the jubilee. Good times, real good times.      You’d have loved the horses in the park, Doris. I used to ride one as a lad. Good for a country boy like me.      Hmm, I remember that estate I taught at, down in Fulham, had a few kids into riding. Now they're all into football and phone games.      Football, yes! Liverpool's still got a good team. Although I don’t know about the new boys. I stick with the old players.      I’d be surprised if you did. I bet you’ve got a few Apple about you as well. I’ve started using the touch bar now, finally caught up.      Oh heavens, you’re all worrying me. I bought one of those electric cars, but   Frank   still thinks it’s evil. Said it's conjured up by the devil.      Ha! I tried an electric one when I went up to Manchester to sell my old bungalow. Rather good once you get the hang of it.      Was it in that road beyond the youth hostel? I remember that place; I stayed there once when I was touring about the countryside.      Yeah, that hostel still stands. I went up last year, selling what little I had left. It’s all in the past really, though.      I had to list mine on eBay, it was the only way I could get rid of them china teacups. I had over thirty to get rid of, bless.      eBay, right, but you’ve got taste, Doris, not everyone’s got thirty teacups lying around.

So did you go and pick up Joshua from your mum’s earlier then?      Yeah, I got there just after she’d fed him. He’d been crying a bit, but he calmed down once he spotted me. Poor thing, I think being at my mum’s all day was too much for him.      Aw, he’s just missing his mummy and his Nana. You’ve only been away for two days! Honestly, I’m so jealous you’re with him all the time. Todayclid’s been feeding me the most bizarre baby mash-up, like apples with peas.      Oh no! Don’t tell me you let someone feed him that hippo mess again! Last time Myra came around with that melon and cumin combo, he was crying for half the day.      Oh, relax! That was an experiment, and it died very quickly. I learned my lesson. I just stick to carrots or bananas now. Honestly, I pity the poor people who have to deal with those baby books that tell you to mix everything in—veggies with fruit, meat with dairy, it’s absolute madness.      I still don’t get why you’ve still got the job when you’re doing it. I thought when you got maternity leave, you were just… you know, off, and not swiping screenshots of baby’s first time eating spinach in black and white for the hundredth time.      It’s not that bad, although someone at work laughed at me when I said my boss wants me to run a conference on baby-talking. Also, I had to explain to a researcher what a “peekaboo” is, and it took nearly ten minutes. I finally sent them a video from Facebook of my cousin’s kid going mental over a teething ring.      I’m still not doing any of that when I come back. I’m just hiding in my house with Josh and a baby monitor and pretending the world doesn’t exist. My youngest cousin said he used to cry when I played The Wombles while changing him. I had to delete it off my phone.      That poor soul! They need to be wrapped in The Wombles from birth. Seriously, I told my sister that go-to formula doesn’t work if you don’t play at least one catchy folky album in the background. It’s the background music that babies crave, your lot forget that.

Rather annoying isn't it, the weather.      You’d think by now we’d have got the hang of it. First the heatwave and now it’s positively chilly again.      Not to mention wet outside. I bet the garden’s like a mossy bog again.      That’s if the cat hasn’t already dug it all up. Speaking of which, I should probably clean out the cat litter before I go.      Can someone else do it while you’re at the clinic this morning? I’m not keen on being responsible for a feline crime scene.      Look, the cat’s only doing her job. Being a My Mini Me mistress is hard work. She left another paw print on the TV screen last night. Darcy, I thought I told you the cat’s not an interior decorator.      She is a menace at times, but she’s taken in every lost pigeon, squirrel and oversized beetle that’s ever crossed the garden. Should have been a gardener instead.      Honestly, I’d rather clean up after her than struggle through a week with her high and mighty attitude. She only remembers her lap when it’s time for treats.      Let’s just say it: she’s a bit of a drama queen. But she’s the only one around here who still listens to me at 8 am.      That’s probably because you arrive at full volume. Morning blaring: a real bonding experience.      Only for the people who mind. Now then, mouths full? Can we all make a plan for the day? I’ve got a 10 am shift, the gardens need tidying, and I’m not doing the bins again.      I’ll do the bins, but I do need a hand for the garden. Unless you’re offering to help, Dad.      If I was younger, I might’ve taken that as an indirect complement. As it is, my back protests at the idea of doing any sustained crouching.      I’m thinking about going over to the clinic a bit earlier this morning. I’ve got an interview go over my on-call shifts if that’s okay with you two?      Of course. And Darcy, can you make sure your cat isn’t in the clinic visiting dogs or something? We don’t need another mix-up with the cat meds like last time.      She’s strictly a private nurse from now on.

So did you get your science results back yet? I’ve been dreading it all week.      Yeah I did yesterday. I got a 6. Not bad, I think. What about you?      I got a 5! Ugh. But it was my second retake and I  still  messed it up. I just can’t get my head around chemical equations. I’ve asked my older brother to help me this weekend, though. He said he’d rather chop off his little toe than do homework again, but okay.      That’s dedication right there. I still can’t believe you’ve made your brother do that. What’s he, like, eighteen and about to go to university?      Yeah. And I’m persuading him via the emotional blackmail method, which basically just involves me sobbing at the table in front of him and saying I'll plant my face in a stamp collection again if he says no.      Don’t tell me, you still do that. I remember the time you buried your head in Waterlow’s Antarctic Stamps book for like ten minutes and I thought you were actually dying. We still credit you with finding two rare ones, though. You are kind of a stamp wizard in our house.      Mate, I got a gift, and I take it seriously. But back to school—what about tests? We’ve got that maths one next week and I don’t even know what they’re asking this time. Ratios, algebra, maybe quadratics again? It just feels like it's never going to end.      I feel you. I’ve been trying to sneak in as much Ed Sheeran as I can while I revise. I know it sounds weird, but it vibes. "Photograph," "Hearts Don’t Break Around Here"—all classic revision soundtracks.      Oh yeah, you’re not alone in that. My friend Aimee told me she listens to Christmas songs on loop during study sessions. She says it makes her feel like time is passing faster and that exams end quicker.      Do you think she actually passes exams or do they just end fast because she’s trying to get to the tinsel?      Good point. Anyway, enough about boring stuff. How’s your mum's garden? I remember she was planting a bunch of tulips and whatnot. She’s like a planting wizard.      Yeah, she is. She’s added some new plants this year—she made me help carry over this huge pot from the greenhouse.

Rather annoying this new bus route they've introduced, isn't it, Ethel? Me hop ‘n’ skip all the way from Costessey now because the new one don’t pick up where the old one did.      Oh, I know what you mean, James. It was fine when I used to run the childminder service, but now I reckon it’s near impossible to get a bus that goes straight through to Harrow without changing! I got to be careful with my eyes as it is—my GP says I'm due another check-up. Didn’t even want to test me at first, said I was too old!      That’s the problem with progress, Ethel. You get older and you expect things to stay the same, but no—the world just keeps turning. I had to explain all this to my granddaughter the other day when she was making a scene about the old rat puppet we used at ceilidh nights!      The rat puppet! Aye, I remember that, Ken. Still got it about? Used to give me a right laugh when Ethel made the thing dance like it was trying to escape out of the window.      It was deadly! I might’ve sewn on a bit extra fur over the years, but it still looked like a cross between a rat and a stuffed teapot. Still, mind you, the kids used to love it—better than the handbell ringing we tried one year at the village fete! That business was someone’s full-time job!      Aye, handbell ringing. You’d think something’d be easier than church bells, but no—got to follow all the same rules, rings, and inversions. I used to run the show when the church needed extra help. Still, I suppose what you love, you’ll keep doing.      I suppose so. I do miss a bit of handbell action, but these days I prefer a nice cup of tea and a bit of gossip. Though I do miss the old days of bus travel. You could always get a seat, didn’t have that rushing-around nonsense now—routes updated with 'improvements,' as they call it!      Aye, I had a row with the driver the other go. Told me he had to cut speeds down so he could "follow protocol." I’m only seventy-three, not a bloomin’ bomb!      It’s all in the name of safety, James.

I can’t believe we actually got a day off to come here. Café Venice was my dream destination since we first came to the North West. It’s about time you saw it properly. I remember this place being full of proper locals when I was a teenager—Ladbrokes would’ve been across the road and there was more of a working-class vibe about the place. Yeah? I’ve only known it as this swanky café with all the artisanal coffee and fancy pastries. I think it’s nice, but was it ever like this? Oh love, not in my youth. It was much more of a no-fuss, no-muss kind of spot. On the weekends you’d get a bit of footy fans passing through after a game at the Macron Stadium, but mostly, it was a place for the school run and local mums with a coffee and a giggle. I still remember the lady at the counter; she’d taken in every lost kid’s homework ever. Ha, I can’t imagine that now. So much has changed since I left here, but it’s still got that small town feel in some corners. Oh absolutely. You’ll still find the best treacle sponge here, and it’s all from the same local bakery at the back. Nothing like the sugary mess you get in other cities. I had a fry-up here once that would’ve put Silvester restaurants to shame. What, they serve breakfast this late? At weekends. You’d order it just before the coffee rush and they’d still serve you a full plate with real fried bread, no skimpy sausages in a Prime Club sandwich. That does sound good. I’m still trying to decide what to get. I’ve never had a proper Venetian-style meal before. You’re not in Italy, for heaven’s sake. But if you want proper food with a bit of class, the lasagne here is bloody good—layered properly, no meaty mess. I could stick to that and a strong flat white any day. I think I might try the battenberg with extra cream. You know I have a slight addiction by now. go on then, but share if you start wobbling. I made my rounds in the morning, so I could go for a bit of sugar, myself. So what’s the plan after this?

So did you go to the gym this weekend? I saw you posted a photo of your squats on Instagram... got to keep up with you, Gemma!      Oh, please! You’re the one who can do a full Turkish get-up at 6am on a Saturday. I just turned up to  not  do my sore back. But honestly, I’m actually feeling better now. Maybe that personal trainer wasn’t just lying when he said I had “undiagnosed posture issues.”      Oh, I  love  that phrase when he says it with a straight face. “You’ve been sitting wrong  this whole time .” What are we, 90-year-old accountants?      So true. I’m not sure if I healed from the posture or from the push-ups I did afterwards. Either way, I feel like a new woman. Although honestly, I haven’t gone past step two of my HiiT routine yet. I keep getting distracted by the jukebox in the changing area. They play  Only You  by The Pretenders like, every other day.      Oh no! I’ve heard that grief. For a minute, I thought they’d replace it with  Gloria , but no—I’m doomed to remember that gym every time I hear either of those songs.      Exactly! It’s gotten to the point where if I hear “Only You” at brunch, I cringe in public. So, how are you doing fitness-wise?      I’m surviving. I’d say I’m in the “I’ve accepted I will never be  that  athletic” stage of my 20s. I’ve started cycling to work again, which is great for my mental health, and failsafe because I can plug my earphones in and listen to a podcast to distract me from the burning thighs.      That sounds like a dream compared to my 9am PowerBlasts at the moment. But I will say, I sort of miss the Saturday night queens and their sprite bottles of water and matching gym bags.      Oh, do you still go out on a Saturday after the gym? I haven’t been to one in months. I think life stopped being a  scene  at some point. Is it just us now, being nostalgic about themed gym parties?      So much so. The last one was karaokes after PowerBlasts, and someone belly-flopped off the stage. Lisa from HR still pronounces “Bohemian Rhapsody” like it’s a medical condition.      Right, right, Lisa who once did burpees in her flip-flops and then fell into the water cooler, right?

Rather skip the new landlord’s nonsense. You know what they do—put up internet speeds and chip in a couple of "luxury extras" and now they want to charge us for something called "energy efficiency contributions." I swear, £20 a month for a fairy light on the landing!      That is a  bouleversement ,   mademoiselle  , as we say in France. I remember when I worked on the archives in Seville, they had a system so archaic, you needed a passport and three pairs of gloves for fragile documents. But, of course, bureaucracy is not a new invention—from Philip of Spain to modern bollards, we are surrounded by it!      My son, bless him, sent me a photo of the new grandchild, born in Lyon—what a special little Parisian in the world now! Living with in-laws, mind you. Wait, does he even speak French? Last time I saw him in Chichester, he was marveling at how the cathedral’s spire was gone. Goodness, I thought—after over 600 years, gone in one gust!      Indeed, and credit to the architect, Porden, though he’d be turning in his grave if he knew how the modern council planned to reclad it with bollards, and none that support the weight of a proper statuette of Mary Tudor! You see, I visited the archives in Castile while researching my latest book—what someone said to me stays with me: “History is a room full of clutter, and Mary was the one who dropped a chandelier and shattered the floor.”      Well, as long as your bollards are artistic. I went to a photo exhibition the other day at the Open Day in Oval—nothing fails like old landlords trying to make a gallery of their car parks. You’re writing something, I hear. Poetic history, no doubt?      Aye, a book—well, a manuscript—on the Austrian battleship disaster. You know, the one where 600 died off the coast of Sicily? And what of your new writing project? Still transcribing the British Library's lost voices, I take it?      Indeed. Though I get distracted by stories like our new French neighbors. Gave us a crock pot and insisted we call it a  roue , what a lot of French people are, if I might say so—full of charm and mildly confused about the roadworks.      Oh yes, and tourists—oh the tourists! A young couple wandered in the other day all wide-eyed at Lambeth Bridge.

So did you lot actually do the geography homework or what? I still haven’t done it and it’s like... due in an hour or something.      Erm, we did start it, I swear. Not all of us, though. Simon from our class actually tried to make coordinates out of M&M packet barcodes. Kept telling the teacher it was his “interpretive homework.”      I think he got one of those social smiles. You know, the one where you’re like,  “Oh, very creative,”  but you literally want to die.      I didn’t do it either. I was too busy at my cousin’s party. There was like a My Chemical Romance cover band, you lot. It’s a lost cause.      Aww, cool! That’s the third best band ever, apart from Blink and Paramore.      I mean, still... I’m not even proud of you, man. You missed out on puffing out the map of Kazakhstan like usual. It’s like one of the few things we’re actually consistent at.      I did mine. I only took two hours. My little brother kept watching TikTok videos and kept asking, “Can I have a geography map on my face with noodles?”      Sounds like my little cousin. He tries to wear my comic books as socks. I showed him the Wolverine comic and he said, “Cool, someone who fights and has a suspiciously clean mouth.”      I showed him the Swamp Thing one and he went, “Eww, gross green vegetables?” I had to explain it’s a comic about cosmic horror... and he still brought a spoon to the dinner table “just in case.”      My little sister barely touches meat now. She said she doesn’t want to eat anything that could’ve watched  Goodfellas  and felt nostalgia. I have no idea where that came from.      My nan is restricting my mac n’ cheese. She thinks I’m “heading to academe and not a barista job.”      I love my mum, but she treats me like I’m going to the Olympics when I go to school on time. I got a gold star for wearing socks with shoes once.      My dad walks around Googling “pros and cons of healthy diets” and then randomly asks me, “Do you think fruit has calories?” like he’s trying to sabotage me.      At least he doesn’t comment on the fact my jeans are probably five sizes too small. My mum just says, “At least it’s trendy,” and leaves the room.

Right, thanks for having us today, Dotty. Happy birthday to Jonathan, love it! He’s like... got the big 12 now, has he?      Oh, yes! Twelve is a right rite of passage, I always say! Grown-ups now, I tell him eeny every single morning!           Can I have a bite? I made one too at school, but this one looks...      flashier?      Here, Jonny, you made one too? That’s nice of you! Not as tasty as Dotty’s, I bet.      Oh My Lord, you haven’t met his new left foot yet, Harry! I made the batch with Darcy, and used that new Fair Trade brand from the shop in Kendal. Tastes better than breakfast, no doubt about that!      The brand at the shop, you mean “Kendal Kuisine” or was it the one with the red logo—?      Oh, that’s not the one I used, no! It was the one with the flower on it. You buy it at the little farmer’s store where Anne works. Dotty is all about the branding now: “Eco, local, and natural.”      Doesn’t matter if it’s eco or not if it’s tasty, eh? I liked the old one best, just plain flour and butter. No need for all that clearing-out nonsense.      Some things never change, Nelly. You still clear out tea bags under the sink after your ballet sessions.      Oh, hush! I’m the one who found the “lost” thimble you said you dropped in ’71! I’m the queen of clearing out in this family!      So, what’s happenin’ after this? Is there a present or something?      There   are   presents, Jonny. I got you a book about queens and kings. Let’s see... here we go. “Queens of the Line: From Boudicca to Elizabeth.”      Boudicca was a goon? I mean, I like her though. She kicked ass.      Oh, don’t go boxin’ up history already, lad. Read the book before you get too clever!      As long as he doesn’t start planning a revolution like some recent studies have.      Or maybe a holiday to Brighton—got my writing job to organise a writing camp. Jonny can come if he wants.      Brighton? Like, with the beach and the arcades?      Yes! And the fish and chips. Not those new fangled healthy ones, though. Real, greasy ones from the best cart on the seafront!      Aye, that’ll fill a stomach and cut off a few hours!

So did you pick your GCSE options yet? I’ve been stressing about it for weeks.      I did last week. I’m doing art, music, English, and double science. What about you?      I’ve got PE, English lit, maths, and design tech. I  really  wanted to do music too, but my advice teacher said it’d be a bit ambitious with all the coursework.      No way? I thought music would be like clarinet and me and you doing the school recital again. Did she not see us blowing the roof off last term with  Grease ?      I know, but GCSE music is more lectures and theory than actual playing. My left hand is allergic to worksheets, to be honest.      Oh, don’t be silly. You’d totally do it if it wasn’t called GCSE. I’ve been thinking, after GCSEs, what’s your dream job again?      I dunno. I like YouTube, so maybe content creation? I’ve got, like, 20 subscribers and a cow who comments every time. I call her  StubbornNegg .      That’s a proper fanbase. I wanna do marketing or PR with a bit of social media because I follow tonnes of bloggers. I reckon I could tell when they’re sponsored.      You literally catch 80 per cent of ‘em. That dress on  FashionByFlo ? Definitely not paid for. I told her in the comments and got a  middle finger  reaction.      Oh, that’s rude. I blocked her. Anyway, have you picked the right GCSEs for job vibes? I’ve been told you need maths for anything that pays more than delivering Tesco online.      True. I’ve got that. My big brother did A-levels in ICT and now he’s a software dev. He says there’s no way you can fail unless you don’t turn up.      Websites and stuff? Do people still need that?      Yeah, but you don’t even know. My cousin’s best friend quit college go work with celebrities cleaning their bogs or something.      Wait, cleaning bogs for famous people? Like baddies and musicians?      I think they’re conference gents in disguise. Either way, she makes like £25 an hour and gets to meet people doing stuff we only see on  TikTok Slang .      My Clarinet teacher says I should do drama college, casting, or something media-related. She swears Leonie used to clean toilets for Harry before she became a stage manager in the West End.

Rather skip the new model entirely. I mean, what is it five years old and it still works just like it used to. Never had no luck with these gadgets. I prefer a good old Land Rover Defender, built to last. Not like some flimsy electric things you see now.      That's true, I used to drive one back in '75 when I was still working on the farm. A lot of muddy fields and no roads to speak of. Oh but the countryside was wild back then. You haven't seen the like nowadays. Massive fields where there are houses now. Probably not too many otters in the river these days either. Gone and been built up.      Oh well the birds still around, I see enough of the magpies when I’m walking the dog. And the squirrels, ooh they’re cheeky. Living with ten children at once and they’re still breakfast, no thank you. I mean, still a bit of wildlife at least, even if not enough hides or reeds for the birds to nest in.      I do tell you, reading up on some of the old battles in Norfolk land. There was this one early Roman battle, can’t quite remember where… something about the Iceni and Boudicca. Not much history about it here, but I read a bit in the local museum. Some of the old Bronze Age earthworks out near Thetford. Bit of a hobby for me now.      Yes, I included a bit on that in my lecture this term. I had the students read about the Fenland excavations, and some of the hill forts near King’s Lynn. Though, honestly, most of them just looked bored. They prefer screenshotting the PowerPoint and quoting it on social media. Honestly, you wouldn’t believe how many university students barely know the difference between a Facebook ad and a news story.      That’s right. I was on that forum the other day, one bloke was arguing that microwave ovens were somehow invented in the 1990s. Like, what? He’s 42 years old with a computer in the house from probably the turn of the century. You think they'd know a thing or two!      But I suppose it’s not all bad. At least they’re into the outdoors, I see the younger ones out with their phones taking pictures of the trees and birds. It’s not much, but it’s something.

Rather skip the queue and just go through the side door, do they?      Oh, bless them, they often mistake it for a more direct route! Poor dears, they mean no harm, just full of good intentions.      Just like the time I tried to take the children to a fancy dress party with one coat handed over to me and the other given to a friend with a note listing all the provisions needed! Of course, it was easier said than done.      You mean the time the children ended up in mismatched outfits? Mummy came out with one half of a space suit and the little boy with the other half?      Oh yes, and then I had to explain to the other parents that this was by design to show the importance of fitting in properly and cooperating in school.      They looked like they were waiting for the Queen of England at this party!      And I had the oversized cape that, unfortunately didn’t fit anyone so I had to wear it myself!      You know, I still get deliverymen rapping gently on the door to this day and say, "Erm, is this the house where the giant cape is kept then?"      Mate, I got misted up and actually had to confirm if they were delivering a sombrero by mistake to my place as well.      Oh that's a good one! They must think this house is a treasure trove of fancy dress leftovers just waiting to be rediscovered.      Or maybe I should be branching out into costume hire!      I about did that years ago! Sold off a couple of the outfits to this man who turned out to be a failsafe for that new school dramatic society.      Oh, do tell!      And then passed them on to his son at the next open day. You probably got one of them talking to witches and stuff on your school grounds.      Oh aye, I recall seeing one with a pointy hat and a long robe wandering the corridors. That's you alright delivering the goods with style.      Mm, that wasn't me. I was too old for such antics back in the day, but I always enjoyed a laugh watching the younger pupils zip about in them.      You know, one of them was even so earnest about acting like a witch that he ended up in hospital with overexertion from running about!      Oh I'm so sorry!

‘Ey Mark, you ain't seen the snow, have yer? I was out in the garden this mornin’ an’ I looked out the window like it were some kind of bloody winter wonderland! It ain’t bin this bad in years, I bet even Grandad wouldn’t argue with it if it een lasted a fortnight!           Yeah, it’s pretty wild. I only had to drive past the side of the university to pick up a couple of things, and someone damn near drove me off the road trying to get up a hill. I’m telling you, if I had to go stag tonight, I’d be snowed in!           Stag? You mean the one you’re doing for Jamie in June? I told him if I had to go, I’d be in a tracksuit and with a flask, cos there’s no way I’m drinking margaritas at this time of year.           You, ordering rum for the first time in your life, and politely—unheard of.      Oh, ha ha! Anyway, speaking of plans, I were thinkin’ we could still book a table at that little French place by the river for the hen. It's got a view of the Cam and it ain’t no swank place, but it’s got somethin’. You know what I mean?      Yeah, that’d work. I just need someone to help me dress the part. God forbid I turn up in one of those flowery shirts you had as kid.           That  would  be unkind. I did make quite the impression back in the day, didn’t I?      Oh, you did. “Sheffield Summer Fashions,” if memory serves.      Anyway! When the snow clears, I’m going to actually start on the garden. I’ve bin meaning to plant some alliums cos I dunno what else to do with the front. It’s looking like a middle-aged man’s mulch pile with a dream.           You mean  your  idea of a dream—which is basically a patch of land with one pond and about seven sun loungers.           You’re bloomin’ marvellous, Mark. So listen, I was thinking, why don’t we do a Come Dine With Me-type thing over the Easter break? We can have a few people over, food, drinks, maybe even a homemade playlist so we look like we done it properly.      Listen, if it’s baked aloo from your recipe, I’m in.

Rather skip the newfit meat eh?      Aye, it's such a muckel of naff, ain't it? It tastes like boiled shoe leather, if you ask me.      You wouldn’t like it, Dad. It’s actually quite decent if you season it properly. I tried the mushroom one with some paprika and garlic.      Oh yeah, that sounds better than the one I got from the supermarket. It was dry as a Norfolk field in July.      I don’t see the point of it all. Why not just eat a fookin’ lettuce?      That’s the spirit! Though I think you’ll find the vegans are the ones who like their greens more than the lot of us!      The idea is to make it taste like meat while being better for the planet. Healthier for us and less harmful for the environment.      And what is wrong with us, then? I’ve never had the fookin’ blues—never been ill a day—personally I think this newfit food lark is a load of codswallop.      Fair point, Dad, but we’re also thinking of the next generation. You remember Mateo talking about the drought in Africa, right? Things like this are part of trying to cut carbon and water usage.      Oh, don’t talk to me about Mateo. He’s always in his room with that book readin' nonsense, playing the world's savior.      Well, I get it’s hard to change habits, but it’s not like we have to give up meat altogether. Just eating less of it can help a lot.      Yeah, I know what you mean. I mean, it’s not like I’m not going to enjoy a Sunday roast every once in a while. But if I can make smarter choices on the other days, it’s all part of being responsible.      Responsible or not, you won’t catch me putting any of that fake stuff in the lunches of my grandkids!      Oh no, you remember when you gave them that "special" dinner of yours, the one with the overcooked cabbage and gravy?      That was a classic, was it not?      Anyway, moving on—for dessert, have you tried the new chocolate and Hazelnut vegan brownie I made?      Oh, yes indeed, and you know I do like a bit of something sweet. You really nailed it!      Totally, I had one earlier, it’s like eating a proper chocolate brownie. I could swear it had butter in it.

Rather annoying isn't it.      Yeah.      The first couple of days I thought she was just being like more anti-social cos she's having a quiet holiday or whatever but now I think she's actually feeling ill.      Yeah I don’t want to go there if I don’t think they want visitors.      Yeah don’t you just feel like when your parents are old and stuff you feel like you're rushing into their house pulling out lots of tins and making them look like this.      Yeah I don’t like to go in if they don’t want it.      Yeah well Alice and like well Myra and I have been going there every couple of days.      You're on the pick and mix every single time aren't you.      Yeah we do, no we actually need to go.      When’s the next time you lot are going to do it.      Month and a half maybe cos we don’t know what's happening with the house I think we're not as quick as we thought.      Yeah I don’t know it's quite a task.      Mate it's got fairly badly, like needs a slap of paint and a clean and new curtains maybe.      If we could get painters in at the weekend, they said it was someone who could just come in.      Yeah well we can do the worst bits like the kitchen and bathroom.      Can I come with you when you do it.      Yeah okay you can help clear the hall.      Maybe paint the doors.      Yeah if you're not in to do something, like for the day.      Yeah.      I'm going to have to take the day off work.      We just need to figure out how to do it cos we've been waiting for ages.      Yeah the kettle's boiling you remember, the last time it boiled it started hissing away go on then switch it off if you don’t want it.      It's okay.      You might get some tea you might not.      Yeah well we're going to try and get someone to help with that like we can't have a broken kettle in the middle of them fitting the new.      Mm.      Water's coming out like it did before you remember when.      It was just like spitting.      Our dad was so proud when he fixed the taps for goodness sake.

So do you think we could pair up our podcasting with some video streaming?      I mean, I've had some luck doing that with the schools I teach at.      Yeah? So we do a topic and then we create a condensed clip that gets put on YouTube and then we link that from the podcast.      Exactly. It helped me with a recent talk I did on cyber policy and international law. I had a few thousand views on the clip and someone reached out wanting me to appear on a panel discussion in Adelaide.      That’s brilliant. We could even make it interactive. Like, after someone watches the clip, they can access a quiz that relates to the topic. It could count toward course credit if you’re a student.      Oh, I love that. It makes it an added incentive to engage with the material. I see students distancing more and more from traditional lectures these days. If we tailor the content to their preferred platforms, we might see more uptake—and maybe even more funding from universities that want to innovate.      Absolutely. And I think if we land a sponsor to support this early on, we’ll have a decent launch. I’ve been looking at some ed-tech services who might want to align with this kind of innovation.      That’s huge. Let me know if you want to write them a proposal. I’d be happy to help with that. I’ve worked in a couple of departments that get grants for educational development.      That would be amazing. We’d need some data or figures to back it up, but I’ve had some key trends in my own start-ups where content-driven strategies pulled in reliable engagement from 18 to 24-year-olds.      So you’re thinking of it as a student-focused product to start with, but with potential for expansion into education for working professionals too?      Precisely. If we create bite-sized content, it can appeal to both demographics. And who knows, if we build that first as a side project, maybe it’ll go viral and we can spin it into a company.      I’d love to see the proposal when it's ready. I might share it with some colleagues at work. Some of my friends in digital learning are always on the lookout for innovative tools—and if what your team is building could be something tangible, it might help us both out in more ways than one.

So did you go out last night or just swot in like normal?      No, I got out for once! Went to this little bar down in Wimbledon—Superdry had a Halloween pop-up thing. You’d have loved it, I mean, it was  loaded  with candy floss and sticky buns, and everyone was in some ridiculous costumes. Someone dressed up as a… well, a "mental health rainbow unicorn."      That sounds like a nightmare. Imagine trying to dump someone in a unicorn costume. “Sorry, my sparkles aren't feeling the glitter anymore.”      Haha! Honestly, I just wanted a quiet night and ended up getting dragged into some kind of dance-along by a group of seven-year-olds. I’m not sure if I’m part psychiatrist or D.I.Y. entertainer in my spare time now.      Poor you! I was just here baking pumpkin bread and trying to plan a kitchen in my head. I keep imagining moving to somewhere, you know, remote. Like Cornwall. Imagine waking up to that cliff view and no one to tell me what I’m doing wrong!      Cornwall’s lovely. I did a placement in a community mental health team there. Killer sunsets, killer workload. You’d want to build a rocket out of cupboards just to escape sometimes.      Yeah, but seriously, I did apply for this project co-ordinator role in the New Forest. Like, they said “flexible hours,” which is code for “we expect you to work 24/7.” But you know, at least I’d be surrounded by deer and silence. Maybe I’d be alright as a lone human in the woods…      You’d probably just end up building a hut and starting a support group for squirrels that are too anxious to cross the road.      That, or overcoding baked goods for them. Baked goods for every occasion. “Low-street sugar scone for anxiety,” “high-fiber gingerbread for restricting.”      You’d be  respected . Also, if you ever do that, I’m coming with you. I’ve had it with hospital induction after induction where someone’s idea of a “team-building exercise” is a group therapy roleplay session.      You’re just not cut out for uniforms and team huddles.      Exactly. So Cornwall or the New Forest, really, and one emergency pizza oven. I can live with that. Just promise me we don’t have to overplan the kitchen.      Deal. I’ll just make one espresso table for our squirrel meetings and call it a day.

Rather annoying isn't it, this weather.      It's been like that all week, nonstop. I had to cancel the trampoline park trip for the kids today.      Oh, shame that. Was it their birthday?      Yeah, it was Harry’s, my nephew. We were going to do that thing with the bouncy castle and a pizza. A real proper party.      Bouncy castle and pizza was my idea of luxury as a kid. My parents were very cheap.      You know what? I actually remember you from school. Mrs. Philips, right?      That's me. My turkey twizzlers were always eaten by someone.      I would never do that! But I do remember sitting behind your desk once and looking for a pencil and finding a chocolate breakfast cereal—Frosted Flakes.      That’s me alright. I hides my snacks to stop you lot eating them. Good job I never shared—your lot ate like you were being knighted.      Was your husband在校任教 back then?      Yes, he was the head of IT in the school. You wouldn’t remember him—he left a while ago.      Oh, I'm sorry. He was quite intimidating when I was at secondary.      He was, wasn’t he? Fierce with computers. He once got a pupil sent home for trying to log into the school email with a dinosaur name.      Really? That’s wild!      I about died laughing. That child was brought round the next week with a homemade logo and a whole mission statement—he even knew how to do headers and footers!      That is brilliant. I’d love to show that to my team at work. They’re always trying to get the kids into something technical. We had this one yesterday, about Archimedes computers. We had to rush a handmade speaker just to get out of it.      Oh yes, I remember the Archimedes set—my husband had one in every room. That was back in the day when your life stopped if the computer crashed.      It’s funny how technical stuff evolves, isn’t it? Anyway, about Harry’s birthday—do you fancy it at your place? We can do high tea with doughnuts and belly dancing from 2 Unlimited?      Belly dancing and doughnuts? I’m in! You lot bring the music and the cake, and I’ll handle the soggy biscuits and peppermint tea.      You legend. It’s sorted, then. Yeah, we’ll text the others.      I’ll make tea while you go, love.

So did you go to the café near the station today? I was messaging you about it earlier.      No, I went to that one down by the university square instead. It had proper croissants. Not like that chain you like in town.      Yeah, I saw the queue there and thought “nah.” But I tried the iced cappuccino from the chain and I have to say—      —you're obsessed now aren’t you? That place is basically just coffee, sugar and plastic cups. But, hey, it's cheap.      Tell me about it. I've got to keep my francs where I can. Speaking of, are you working on that experiment report for biology week?      You're psychic, I was just staring at the graph. I still don't get the percentage deviations. Why do we have to apply that formula again?      Because, you know, in experiments, you have to show the difference between the control and the real data—so you do like, theoretical reading versus what you actually get. I think.      Oh yeah, and then you factor in human error—like how I dropped half a gram of sodium chloride down the sink – twice.      And that was  only  because the tap wasn't closed properly and you were trying to use the scale at the same time with your phone in one hand.      Honestly, I need a lab coat with Velcro pockets. I’m out here like a kid with a science set. Hey, did I tell you about the bands in Angers? We could do a trip there after exams.      Oh yeah, I read a review online about some local indie band playing at some warehouse. It sounded proper up for it—pyrotechnics and everything.      That was ours. I followed them on the student radio show. They were touring the student cities—their singer is waiting till she gets a degree to start proper.      Nice! Do they play a lot of English songs or mostly French?      A bit of both. But the English ones are go-to crowd favorites. One of their songs had a real science metaphor—something about cell membranes and breaking bonds.      Aww, that’s poetic. I’m gonna have to see them live then. We could go down after the project is due, if we survive it.      Only if you promise not to drop a measurement cup on my foot like you did last time.

Rather annoying to wake up and find a load of cobwebs in the corner of my office, especially when it’s got to be spotless for the client today.      Oh, spiders! There’s always one hiding somewhere in my house, especially now it’s getting colder. They make their webs and then vanish like they’ve been there by mistake!      It’s not just a clean issue—they’re so quiet! I had this one crawl across my keyboard last week. It gave me the shivers!      Funny you mention it, I had a mouse the other day too. Horrible little thing ran across the hallway just as I was making my tea. You know, they come looking for crumbs, so I’ve made it a habit to clean up more carefully now—even the bread crusts!      Oh, mice are a nuisance. My cat would have been all over it if she lived here, but no... I only ever had a ginger tom and he treated mice like, well, chew toys—and I mean  every  corner of the house would smell like mouse and cat for weeks after.      Bless him, I had a calico once who would hide the mice and drop them at my feet like a little present. “Mum, look what I got you!” I’d say, but really, I just wanted the mess out of my hallway!      I understand completely! And with that said, I’ve also just had a full song and dance with a magpie in the garden. Keeps stealing shiny bits—buttons, teaspoons, anything it can get its beak on. I had to hide the hubcap, or it would have been nowhere!      Oh right, magpies are notorious for that! My neighbour tells me you are supposed to put out a plate of shiny things near the back to distract them, like a little ransom. Haven’t tried it yet, but it sounds better than me chasing a bird round a garden holding my keys trying to distract it!      We had to do that when I lived in Boston. My grandad used to leave a little “pay-off box” with tin cans and wire things. Said it worked half the time!
