Aye, well not as dramatic as this, love. But when I were a lass, we 'ad t’ devolution of Wales and Scotland. Back in the 80s, I think. It was a long time ago, but somethin’ to remember. People were divided—some folk said we don’t need no principles and parameters in this ‘ere, just get on with t’ government business like we always did.      Does it matter much to people like us? I mean, will it change  our  lives?      Oh, it'll matter, alright. If Scotland votes to go i'the other direction, they’ll need their own t’currency, their own government, their own laws—welfare, ‘ealth, you name it. All that malarkey. And if they leave the EU again... Bless ‘em, it could be a world of pain waiting to happen!      What if they vote  yes ?      Gracious me! That would be the kettle boiling, you could say. Then ‘ow do we divide up the money goin' on in North Sea oil fields? What happens to the Royal navy? To the passport? You don’t go ‘unifying’ when you ‘ave a big border at the north, and all!      Does it affect us here in Yorkshire, do you think?      Yeah, why not? Aye, we’re all part of this great big muddle they call the United Kingdom. But folk up north always like 'aving a go. Just like ‘ow we Yorkshire folk used to have our own laws before Oliver Cromwell came ‘n' sorted out t’ lot o' us, aye!

Oh my God, listen to this bloke's accent! I swear he sounds like he’s got string and clogs on. What part of the States is he from?      He's probably from Alabama or sommat like that, innit? Course he does. He sounds like my old eeny auntie Mary from Birkenhead when she puts on that “posh” accent trying to sound clean. Aww, bless her tho.      Oh, bless me, not this advert again! Why do they always have to show the chase when he interviews the bloke with the hat like three times before even getting to the main show? It's like, are we watching a game show or a MySpace profile?      I dunno, I find Jeremy Kyle interesting in a bonkers sort of way. Like the way he goes "Oh, are we ready for the big breakfast, are we ready?!" Like he's a Game Show host at a Bingo Hall and not a daytime talk show in America.      Yeah, and like how he says "I don’t need a lawyer!" every time someone’s about to cry. It’s like human drama real-time with teleprompters. It’s mental!      Tell me about it! My nan used to love this series, and now I watch it and I swear the show is set in the 90s. Like, what is this man doing with that blazer and the big smile?      And his way of saying “So what’s happening?” – it’s like the universal opener. Whether someone’s suing their mum or their husband’s had a midlife crisis, he’s about to ask them “So what’s happening?”      Honestly, I’ve been trying not to copy that line. My mate Sarah says every time we meet up to do something, like over the phone: “So what’s happening?” And I’m just like,  it’s Jeremy Kyle, mate, it’s not me.       Honestly, the only good bit is that middle bloke whose job it is to hand over the money or the "gift" if the person wins. Still remember that time he had to give a man a car because he caught his wife with his best mate or something.      Oh, yeah, that was mental. That bloke looked like he’d just walked out of a Fatburger commercial and asked randomly, “Want to sign up for a talk show?”      Oh, and where does this guy’s accent go?

Rather annoying isn’t it? The ref’s just given a red card and they’re down to ten men. I swear, I could’ve shot the poor bugger down I was so angry.      Come on, don’t do that, love. You frightened the cat. And it was a bit soft, I admit, but we’ve got bigger problems than football if you reckon that’s the worst thing on your mind tonight.      Oh I don’t know, watching this Premier League nonsense is like knitting a jumper while the house burns down. Remember when we used to get the Olympics on the telly like three times a year?      Yeah, and I spent the summer before trying to knit a MySpace profile cover for you with an Olympic logo. It looked like a fried egg had fallen into a bin and someone tried to make it look like a medal with a biro.      That was a masterpiece and you know it! Haha. But back to the football… I tell you, if we ever have kids—and I know we’ve talked about it—there is no way I’m naming one Laurie after this absolute side of short puts.      Oh come off it, they might go on a winning streak tomorrow. For all we know, we might be booking flight tickets to Qatar next year. I wouldn’t mind that myself—exotic locations, expensive champagne, telling people that my PhD topic is saving the planet while my team wins every game. It’s the perfect life.      Yes! That’s the attitude. Besides, we can always buy out the stadium and kidnap the ref and then send him an invite to our knitting circle. That’s how we roll in about five years time after we’ve had our baby and the first round of antenatal scans and you’ve given up research for good.      You think I can step away from science like that? I’ve got a paper due next week about the weather patterns at 60 degrees latitude and the effect on pottery distribution in North America. I can’t just knit a scarf while my kid eats lichen off the wall.      You keep telling yourself that. But I do wonder, if our kid ends up being a massive football fan—which they might given how goonie I get—their first word might be “goal” or “stripey socks” or “sit down you’re causing a scene.”

Right, I just wanted to bring up the request that you do everything you can for the child's development. I got the email from the child minding service so I could forward it on.      I don’t think we do anything specifically for the children at our house. We just make sure they’re not eating too much sugar and then they go to sleep on time.      But I saw that Aunty Phoebe got this voucher for participating in the kids' education programme, which is part of why we need to do the vitamins. Didn’t you get one?      Not to my memory. I mean, I don't forget important things, but I haven't received anything like that.      Mmm, maybe it's not just about the vitamins – I think the programme is more for things like school visits and stuff. But if it’s free and gets better results, then it's probably worth trying.      Oh, the teacher mentioned the Queen awards one, you know, for the Royal Fruits Festival? They give out medals to kids who do the most reading in a month. Might be worth keeping an eye out for.      That sounds fancy. Would they even be allowed into a palace if they won?      Probably not the ones with the real, like, swank rooms and huge gardens unless it's an open day, but they might have tea in the big hall or something! Though if we were a Republic, someone said in one of the books they read, like a teacher, then we’d definitely not have palaces to go to.      The Bee Movie said that bees are in charge of the most important things on Earth. Maybe if the kids win the award, they’ll become Queen Bees.      Oh that movie is so old and it is a classic. Remember that scene where they talk for like four hours straight about pollen?      And at the end the bee is holding the sword, like he could be King Arthur!      That’s such good insight. I remember being 12 and trying to draw the bee on the sword with the royal crest and almost setting the paper on fire.      I think the kid go to a palace once, if you count the Royston one.      Oh, yes – the one where the Queen’s portrait had all those scrolls. It was like The Bee Movie but with Romans and tapestries.

Rather skip the queue and just go through the side door, do we?      Oh, lass, it's no’ like they run out o’ tea by lunchtiem!      Charming as the side door sounds, I wouldn’t dream of it. Got eenough to worry about without sneakin’ round like a mug of lukewarm dandelion tea.      Ayup! Proper queue, innit? If you don’t queue, you don’t get cake.      Right, right. Let’s just get our usual. Two teas, one with milk—      And a scone with jam and clotted cream, no sugar. Still, who am I to argue? Ten more years and I’ll be asking for peppermint and fig in mine.      You’ve got time yet. I still can’t believe you’ve never had peppermint in your tea. People’s lives are so complicated these days, ordering lattes with a hundred instructions.      Naa, lattes are too posh. I like my tea leaves as they come. Pa only drinks builder’s today, but he says it’s the proper way.      Let’s talk about something besides tea. I heard they’re clearing the old Miller barn in Thirsk. It’s got proper potential for events if someone’s got the nous for it.      Ooh, an event—sounds like a way to line someone’s pocket. I’d buy a table just to see it go up in sparks and smoke.      Aye, and most people about would fall about if a hen party bled into the stag night and someone brought a goat.      Not you! I’m thinking of a proper gastro evening—think of the farmers’ stalls, the local guest speaker, the tragedy about the weather.      What was he saying about the weather? Wet, I bet. Like always. We had to clear out the garden last weekend. Got halfway through and the clouds came a-callin’.      That’s how you know it’s spring in these parts. One minute it’s July, the next it’s February. If it wasn’t for the brambles, I’d swear they’d stopped growing altogether.      Now that you mention it, I’ve been writing a piece about the absurdity of local weather patterns for  The Kendal Times . Got a bit over the line when I compared them to the NHS. Scheduling my GP appointment is like booking into a pop concert.      You're not wrong, laddie. My doctor’s not used to seeing me, and now I’m seeing a man in a hat who thinks I have a tumour because I mentioned a ‘tweak’ on my knee.

‘Ey luv, you’ve bin scrollin’ through that museum thing again, haven’t yer?’      Maybe. I was just thinkin’ we need an actual date where we don’t do the same £20 takeaway in front of Netflix again. Just like a proper night out, y’know?      Yeah, I know what yer mean. But last time we tried goin’ anywhere, we got stuck in this ridiculous queue for parking and it ruined the whole vibe.      Oh, I got it this time. Apparently, the museum’s under the new £2 parking scheme, so if we go after 5, we pay nothing, and they’ve got free entry on the first Saturday of the month too. Win-win.      You’re obsessed with money-saving, ain’t you? Fair enough though. I’m just tired of the old gig. Wait breakfast, wait for parking, wait in line for a docent — all while I’m thinkin’ we should’ve just stayed in and watched Game of Thrones for the hundredth time.      We need a bit of culture, Sean! Plus, it’s bound to be quieter when the grandmas aren’t there. I was reading the reviews – it’s got a new modern art wing and – Mate, have you been looking at property sites again? You’ve been hovering over that flat in Sefton Park like it owes you rent.      Maybe. Dunno. Our lease is almost up and this place is startin’ to feel like a borrowed flat. I’m thinkin’ of upping sticks, you know? Find something that’s ours, not just someone else’s investment property.      That’s not a bad idea. Although, I have to be honest, you and property? You once got exorcism stickers on the bathroom ceiling for fun.      Hey, that was a statement against damp! A bold one. But honest to god, if we get a flat with a garden, I’m getting a cat. I’m not being funny, as soon as we have to walk more than two steps outside to keep the cat from running away, we’ll wish we’d just stayed in this run-down but dog-free place.      You think it’s that easy though? Just one cat and we’re in? I’m not even pregnant and you’re already planning our wedding invites and kid’s birthday party theme.      You’re not helping. And I never said we were planning a焱宠物派对. I’m over this, anyway.

So did you watch The Rings of Power weekend? I stayed up way too late watching it and I’m  still  tired today.      No I haven’t gotten round to it yet! Got to keep up with all my uni stuff and TikTok says half the show is just slow walking elves and wind.      Yeah, but I reckon it looks so good… like, I mean obviously I love any fantasy stuff, so this is right up my street.      Oh you and your fantasy shows! I swear half your Instagram is just Game of Thrones memes and pictures of like, Arya Stark holding a sword.      Hey, that was  me  in My Chemical Romance when I was 15. I’m not just a fantasy nut – I’m a nostalgic, multi-talented goddess.      Yeah yeah, ‘multi-talented goddess’. You couldn’t even remember to put on deodorant this morning.      Excuse you, I was in a rush, okay?! I was trying to get to this new café in East Ham for brunch that’s supposedly got the best calzone in London.      Real talk—what even is a calzone? Like, is it just a pretentious pizza pocket?      No way! It’s like a folded pizza. All that cheesy goodness wrapped up in a beautiful, flaky dough blanket. And they put chilli aioli on there. It’s suspiciously good.      Okay, now you’re talking my language. Chill aioli sounds  intriguing . I need to try it, but I’ve got about five essays due next week.      Oh come on, one lunch date can’t hurt. Life isn’t all about deadlines and existential dread. Remember last weekend? We just stayed in for 24 hours eating pizza and watching  Phineas and Ferb ?      I watched  Phineas and Ferb  with a 20-year-old and I’m being academically-traumatized.      Okay, but the ferret emoji you sent after the episode? Proudest moment of my life.      Don’t pretend like you didn’t send me like ten separate rants about how Disney needs to reboot  The Lion King  properly.      That was a  valid  cultural critique! And_ratings are never going to reflect the artistic merit of Lion King 2019 anyway.      You know my cousin got to see the live music version in Manchester and he sobbed the whole time? He said it was magical.      Wait, did he cry before or after the stage caught on fire?       That  was intentional. The guy who played Simba had a technical flame prop and it…

So did you watch the Pikachu episode of  Daddy Pig  last night?      No, what happened? Did they go on an adventure or something?      Yeah, it was sweet. Pikachu tried to speak like Daddy Pig so he wouldn't be sent back to his box. It was kinda sad but funny.       Pika… pika?       Oh no! Look at you! You're starting to speak in Pikachu like it’s a second language now.      He’s just copying us isn’t he?      I swear if I start speaking like Chewbacca tomorrow, it won’t surprise me. Just keep talking to him like a normal person, okay Oisin?       Chewbacca?       Yeah, you’re better off learning proper words than that. Although mastering “raining cats and dogs” might be too advanced for you.      Well, he’s got you for that—your vocabulary’s questionable, but it’s educational.      Right, as if I didn’t have enough on my mind. I was thinking—maybe tomorrow we could go to that new Ramen place near school?      You mean the one with the long queue and the chilli oil?      That’s the one. I’ve heard it’s amazing and the portions are huge.      That sounds good, but only if we can do it with a takeaway for Oisin. Or maybe we can take him in a sling?       Ga, ga!       He said “ga.” That means “go,” right? So I think he’s agreeing with us. He just wants noodles for dinner.      Well, if that’s the case, I say we plan it. Do you want to come meet me there or can I sort out the food and bring it over?      I’ll meet you there and bring Oisin. I’ve got a few things to do, but I can make it if I get the day goin’. I’ll see if I can meet you at one?      Perfect. And we can maybe grab an ice cream after if we’re not too full.       Mm, mm       Look at you, fancy man. Are you trying to go all fancy like your Dad with his slippers and weird podcast raps?      Oh, he’s got the whole style down. I just showed him before dinner.      You what now?      I told him, “Rap about Ramen, Oisin. You wanna eat Ramen, you gotta rap it.” So he’s off now.  Da da da da-ramen!       That sounds like my ex. Women like that, apparently.

Rather annoying this, really. I’d rather be hanging out with glue sticks and spider crabs than having to go through all this dusty old stuff. Look at that box—it’s covered in cobwebs. I feel like we’re about to find some ancient, long-forgotten treasure.      Oh come on dear,  this  is the treasure! Remember when we were little and all we wanted for Christmas was that ‘Bako’ set? Such a big deal, right? We used blocks to build a whole damn house! Put a wasps’ nest under the dining table, or so Mummy said.      Oh yes! And I still remember the toy garden spade—entirely useless unless you were digging a hole for your Cabbage Patch kids. And you pretending you were a real gardener, with imaginary pickles growing in our patchwork blanket. It was all about the drama back then, wasn’t it?      Haha! I think we might still be the only people in Kent qualified to do both flower arranging and microscopic slug eradication by that point. I do miss the satisfaction of tidying a place up, don’t you think?      It’s not satisfying today, though. It’s just painful. I’m getting dust puffs in my hair and my back’s been bugging me since I tried to de-clutter the shelves the other day. It’s enough to make you wish for a large dose of back pain cream and a sense of satisfaction in equal measure.      Just don’t fall like Mummy did when she was trying to fling the old curtain rings into the charity bin. Still in hospital because she  thought  she was being agile.      Ugh, true. I still haven’t forgiven her for thumping me with that ‘grandmother’s lace’ box when I was clearing the hall closet. I nearly lost a whole weekend nap just dodging that.      A bit of me says the weather is holding out just to make sure we don’t stop now. You know, raining all day to force you inside. Though I’ve seen worse. At least it’s not the gales we had last week when our shed exploded like a poorly packed firework.      That gothic bin on your porch nearly suffocated me with old newspapers and half a frozen marrow. I swear it had a life of its own.      So, have you made peace with the ‘Bako’ set yet? I can never bear to throw anything that might stir a memory, even if it is covered in green mold and missing 70% of its pieces.

Rather annoying isn't it? The amount of swarms of mosquitoes we've had this summer. I thought they’d got the memo it was no longer the 1970s by now      It's honestly relentless. No matter where we go it's like they have a map coordinates of our skin and they just go to town      Yeah I had to put socks on my hands just to go out to get the bins this morning. They were going after my eyes as well      Oh was that the mosquito or the midge, or the combination of the two?      No, I think it was the midge, only they’ve decided to team up with the mosquito. I’ve never seen anything like it      I know what you mean, I was thinking of taking the little one to the park for a bit of fresh air and breakfast, but I almost need to put her in a bubble in case she gets eaten      Actually the park near the old town hall isn’t too bad, I was over there yesterday, and had one or two, but I put on some citronella to be safe and only got two bites. Whereas in the local country park I got ten      Excellent, thanks – I’ll take her there then, and actually it's a good thing because the weather is perfect.      You know what the best bit is? The weekend gig they have in the park      Yeah, my friend told me they have some really good independent bands playing      I think next weekend is their big headliner as well, so there might be a few more people there      Oh really? Who is it?      Some old indie band you probably won’t have heard of, but my stepdad is a massive fan. I might go with him      I’m open to a wide variety of genres but give me some advance warning so I can pack the right sort of playlist      Haha, good idea.      So what are the traffic conditions like going over there?      Honestly it's a nightmare at the weekend really on the main roads. It does get so backed up      Hopefully it's cleared a bit now that it’s the middle of the week. I have to get into town on Friday and I dread it      You might want to consider a different route or get over there earlier. We had a friend who swore by the back road near the motor museum and they said the traffic was much lighter

So did you get the post today? You know, the one from the careers office—the one they said was a proper graduate role, not some bouncer at a nightclub?      No, nothing yet. I left the house before the post came through at 11 again. Do you want me to check when I go out later? I was just about to go for a walk actually. The physio said I should start moving more before the next exam.      Yeah, go for it. You’ve been inside all week and it’s November. It’s not even Halloween yet—we saw the shop shelves already changed! Anyway, I had a pretty dull day out on the course. It was windy and the turkey curry I had for lunch made me feel like a ghost flew over my head or something. Dizzy, you know?      Oh no, was it dodgy? Wait, you didn’t actually go to the restaurant with the funny sign, did you? The one by the motorway, the one I told you looked like a Christmas advert gone wrong—vibrating lights, a Christmas tree in September—      Yeah, that was it. It wasn’t that fancy, but it was cheap. I tried the garlic naan. Wasn’t too bad for lunch.      So it wasn’t a huge disappointment then. Any better than the staff canteen at uni?      Absolutely. At least the food feels someone cares. That said, the toilets there made me consider just not playing the game. You ever seen something that out of order in the real world? The seat looked like it had a ballet career or something.      I don’t even know where to start with that. Honestly, I’ve been trying not to worry about the future and just focus on the job searches, but it’s tricky, especially with the messages. My sister texts me at 2am sometimes just to tell me the world is ending.      That’s how my little sister started when I told her about my golf internship offer being cut. Next thing you know, she’s Googling "Can you survive solely on Manchester pizza bagels and air."      Yeah, go Manchester. I mean, if you end up working there, at least the line is decent. Hopefully, they don’t send me somewhere like Bognor Regis.      Bognor Regis is okay. I heard the people there like singing along to songs on the telly and over-fermented food.

Okay Aaron, new word: A. You know what A is. Say A.      Aaaa!      Huh, not bad for a nearly-four-year-old. Come on, alphabet runs deeper than the Shannon. B!      Okay, but don’t forget, he’s still got one letter down. That’s more than your cousin Niall managed before he moved to Sligo.      Oh yeah, he was still pulling “J” and calling it “Jiggle” when we last saw him.      Bbbb!      Well, listen to the little Corkman. You’re beginning to sound more like a Reagan than a Rehan!      Okay, A, B and I think he just screamed at the telly again about the cat falling into something.      Which cat? Huh, which cat? I missed the part where we got a cat.      That would be the one you saw three months ago and said, “Oh, let’s put two adoption ads out as a joke.” And then real life followed.      Cc – Coo!      Co?      No, no, no. C is “Cee.” Now don’t go making him say Silly Billy lines.      Oh please, you just wanted a full house of nightmares.      Besides, we should probably talk about dinner. Do we have enough in the way of being able to feed a toddler  and  a fully functioning adult who about five minutes ago was eating the goldfish from the bowl?      We can rustle something up. Breaded chicken, boiled potatoes, a bit ofཀ green. That should satisfy us all.      And Aaron can have the chicken without the breading. And probably the potatoes either.      You mad? My tummy’s gone as tight as a player’s bicep trying to catch a cricket ball in the heat.      Still trying to live off your glory days in the English league?      Oh please. If it wasn’t for me, you’d still be living off Marmite, toast, and arguing about your iTunes playlists at two in the morning.      That was once. And it was under duress from your dad on the phone going “You’re pronouncing Cee-wick like a monkey!”      Cc!      Listen, Reg, keep that up and we might make a mini-language teacher outta you. But maybe you won’t. Maybe you’ll turn out just like your Uncle James, last seen buried in a pile of recorded BBC Three repeats.      Now that’s a terrifying legacy.      Next thing you know, he’s got his own online university teaching “how to dance like Adele at a Coras Varach Women’s Club karaoke night.”

Right, I swear I dreamt I was sat at my desk filling out forms in my pants again last night... What's up with that?      I know, I've noticed you've been doing it more since we came here. Look, it's called a holiday. You can lie in your boxers and pretend you're on a tricycle in the garden if you like.      Ha ha, very funny. Honestly tho, this isn't funny. I keep seeing myself as some sort of underwear CEO. It's not me. Is this the jet lag, or the fact we came to a village three times smaller than my office?      What’s a CEO?      My job, Elise. I’m the pants-based boss of pretending to be important.      Oh cool! Can I be your pants assistant?      Go on then. She can hand you the stapler. Honestly though, I think it’s the house. It’s too quiet, too old. You get lost in your thoughts.      Can I have a stapler?      Not yet, Harry. Staplers are for when you can hold a book without dropping it three times.      Right, but let's not talk about me wearing pants all night, I want to talk about extending the house. I’ve been thinking about that again.      Right, so you’re not the only one stuck in a dream state. I’ve also been dreaming about a house with walls that stretch like sourdough bread.      Well, imagine this being split in two – a bigger kitchen, a second living area, maybe even a place for us all to not step on each other’s toes during breakfast.      Can we have a room for my dinosaurs?      I want a slide!      Okay, note to self: slide. And maybe a tunnel. I'm already planning a wooden slide and a basement digout for them.      As long as we can still pretend we live in space by the kitchen window. That window is my main psychological connection to the universe.      You're like a man-baby with gothic aspirations. But yeah, maybe some kind of glass conservatory.      With green plants. Real ones, not the plastic ones your mother used to use to fool the flu.      Fair enough. And maybe solar panels?      Is it too much to imagine this dream home running entirely on natural light and a homemade windmill?      Can the windmill spin like my toy one?      I want the wind to blow up!

Rather skip the new chaise longue I think, Ahmed. I've had it in my sights for a few months and I thought I'd surprise the family at Christmas. But now I've found out that a water main burst behind the new garden wall, and the garden's a bit like the moon’s surface at the moment.      C'mon, Dai, it's not as if they don’t break down every now and then. That old system’s got to be at least thirty years old, pulling through it. We’ve had the same thing happen at the uni when they upgraded the building. Had to fetch water three times a day!  Swansea!  All we needed was supply and another row with the company.      Oh, you talk like it’s normal. I told the water company and what do they say? I quote:  “Due to unforeseen circumstances, we can’t prioritise breakfasts and pergolas at this time.”  Haha! And don’t get me started on their customer service, it’s like they think a database is optional.      Blooming bureaucrats—personally I think they'd be better off with a particle accelerator to unblock human bureaucracy than the LHC in Geneva. At least we’d get something out of it. Tell you what, at least your garden won't be watered by the council for a while, so the mint and the apple tree will suffer equally and at least be fair.      Fair, huh? Our mint is currently in an argument with gravity. That stuff grows like it just graduated from the particle collider— expansion at near light speed . Anyway, being back on topic: I  would  spend the money on a chaise longue. Just not now. But talking of spending, I had an email from Ron yesterday—he got approval for that data ethics funding project. Published it under  Contemporary Applied Ethics and AI , for goodness sake. Got guest speaker status at Oxford.      Ha! I'm told it was all down to his intense PowerPoint. I mean, he convinced the funding committee to trust him over physicists. That’s a real accomplishment. And what about your new paper with the collaboration from Pisa? That's set to deliver something amazing.      Yeah, go me. I'm hoping if we publish soon, maybe I can go to Rome in the spring, between snow and mud, and stay in a hotel where they still serve coffee at 10 am instead of kibble and tap water.

Right, I swear I haven't seen the purple Duplo pieces anywhere. You’d think they'd just  vanish  rather than be anywhere obvious, wouldn’t you?      Mmm, I don’t think we had any purple Lego. Maybe Grandad gave us some from his old box?      Or maybe they’re   INVISIBLE!        Ha! A lot of use that'll be when I’m trying to clean up. Right, while I hunt for those, can you two tell me what you’re working on, then? Still building your Hogwarts?      Not anymore. I’m making the Ministry of Magic now. With secret doors like in the movie.      Oh good one. What about you, love? You building something special?      Yeah! It’s the pizza shop from Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles. I’ve got all the purple for the bad guys and the green for the turtles hides, see?      That’s brilliant! I like how you’ve got the pizza boxes on the roof—very realistic. You’ve been watching that show again, haven’t you?      Ugh, it’s on in the afternoons. It’s actually quite good. Mikey channels, like, pure slapstick comedy.      Mikey’s silly and Silly was what I said! Silly! Silly! Silly! Silly! Silly—      Oh, for goodness' sake! Okay, yes, Mikey   is   silly and being silly is great fun   AS LONG AS   you’re not shouting about it at 5 PM on a Tuesday.      Honestly, I miss watching  The Simpsons . I don’t  grumble , I just have a word with it and it apologises politely. That’s what people do in my time.      And you’re the talking wall of this house, so they take you seriously.      Right, I’m phoning up for that man from the local electrician. I’ve got that list of jobs he did for me last time.      Oh, I remember that — he took you ten minutes to sort out a crack plug and then had a cup of tea out the back. Proper lunches on a job site, ha!      Do you think he can rewire the whole place while he’s goin’ on? Cos if he’s there, might as well ask him to tickle the wall sockets.      Aye, and maybe fit some nice hot water pipes too, why not? It’s all about voltage and conductivity and you-      Ah, go on, you're on one of those science binges.

So… we were watching  Peter Pan , and your fairy godmother made all the birds fluiey?      Fluiey? She made the birds  fly , Charlie. Rather annoying isn’t it, eh? You know, spending ages in the car just to get through the first few miles and then it's all luck whether you run into traffic or not. I’m planning to make special trips to see everyone after Christmas. I’ve never been to Cornwall, so I might take the kids for a few days at the end of the holiday.

Rather a lot of people taking a rest today, isn't it? I was just down by the track—seems the weather’s put them off a bit more than I'd expected.      Aye, well, we do what we can when we can. Oh, it’s meant to be bloody brilliant—Policy speeches, exhibitions, you name it. I hope they’re not just going to let middle-aged men ramble on about the 'good old days,' you know. Not if the recent trends are anything to go by. I’ve had a couple of my ex-colleagues on about it, and none of them are exactly feminist trailblazers in the making, I’ll say that.      Aye, you see that in the big firms, don’t you?

Mum, I just wanted to go through our plans again for the holiday—it's in three weeks, right? I’ve got your number in my phone and a list of things you said you wanted us to do—like the local museum walk and the little pond with ducks you always talk about.      Oh, I remember that! Nan used to feed the ducks when I was a kid.

So did you watch the Euros last night? That Bruno Fernandes goal was absolute madness, innit?      Aye, I saw that. I was at a friend’s place, we were all screaming. Not quite like a Barbadian cricket match, but close.      Haha, yeah, we don’t get much cricket over here. My cousin actually tried to explain a T20 game to me last week and I just got lost halfway through.      That’s one of them games where the numbers get too much when you don’t grow up with it. I still remember when I first came over and I thought "over" was like, you know, over like water.      Oh my gosh, I just died laughing when you told me that. But anyway, I think I turned your cousin onto Euro hockey now. She’s been texting me asking about stick skills and all this stuff.      Blooming hell. I hope she’s not planning on challenging the men’s national team over here or nothing like that. She knows I play for the company, right? I don’t need no drama.      You’ll be fine. She’s watching YouTube tutorials, so it’s all pretty humble. Although, she just bought a new helmet and stick, and I think the total came up to like, thirty quid.      Oh, thirty? That’s not bad for a starter. Our gear here tends to cost a fortune. I had to buy a new pair of boots because the laces split in the middle of a game and I ended up tripping. Cost me the best man spot in my cousin’s wedding.      That’s rough. What did you do to get a freebie boot outta it?      Nuffin, but my boss just laugh ‘cos he was playing in that same game. Said he was distracted and missed the winning goal. Doesn’t matter ‘cos I got a new pair anyway.      Blokes are always like that. Let’s be real, you were probably dreaming of new boots anyway.      You think I would’ve come this far if I didn’t know how goaldust my lifestyle is? Nah. I’m real serious about this, even if I’m only in a team of boxers and salesmen.      Well, I’ll be your personal fan, then. As long as I don’t have to go to any matches and stand for two hours in the rain like at them sporting events I once went to with my dad.

Rather skip to the moonlight type thing innit, me leg’s feeling a bit stiff after that walk. I got to take it easy on the bad side, eh? Not like I used to. Back in my day we were runnin’ ‘cross the fens wi’ a stone in our boot if it een’t harm us, eh?!      Oh, Bill, you’ve always been a bit of a showoff when it comes to that! I don’t think anyone’d expect you to sprint across the fens now you’re in your dotage. Didn’t your doctor say you should be walking more slowly, not more quickly?      That’s the problem with us old folks, Alice. We always think our bodies should work like they did fifty years ago. But Bill, I’m with Alice—take it easy, and I’ll get the tea made. It is, after all, the proper thing when you’ve been strolling about in the rain.      Aye, I remember that, Ken. Tea’s the cure for anything. I reckon we’d all be better off if we had a proper cup of it every hour instead of that sugary sludge they sell in the shops now. Taste like they’ve boiled a washing machine.      Tell me about it—heard about the new holiday centre opening in Yorkshire, it’s supposed to be all the rage. Youth hostels and all, for the young’uns. Not sure what they see in them places, but at least it keeps them off the television.      Aye, I took one of my classes to a similar place a while back. Bit crowded, but the kids had a laugh. Although, most of them couldn’t find north if it hit them on the head. We were using a globe in the classroom and one of them said it was ‘just spinning like it didn’t care’.      That’s the lot of them. All passed out on their phones and no idea where the Earth is going. I remember us trying to grow a vegetable patch for a school project. We had to clear the overgrown land ourselves. These young’uns probably wouldn’t touch the ground with a bargepole.      I did a bit of that with the kids I looked after. They were fascinated by growing their own food, but give them a brussels sprout and they’d rather eat mud, I swear.      It’s all part of the learning curve.

So did you manage to sort out those flights to Edinburgh for Sarah’s hen do?      Barely. I had to email the airline like six times before someone actually replied. It’s a mad scramble at the last minute with only two weeks to go!      Yeah, I saw the prices sky-rocket the second I opened the website. I reckon we’ve paid enough for a week’s stay in a flat just to get this lot sorted.      Honestly, someone should invent a time machine just so us women can book travel when it’s still  sensible . I like to think of it as  early booking , not  last-minute chaos .      It’s a good job Sarah’s hotel has confirmed the group booking. Ten of us in one hotel—it’s either a party or a sleepover turned nightmare. Or most likely both by the end of it.      I mean, with a hen do, it’s usually both. Last year we went to Manchester, and the first two days were like a campsite—set up, shop, get drunk, collapse. Then the last two days we were dressed as tartan highland cows for a photo session. Legend.      Oh right, someone told me that. I remember thinking it looked like a real shindig.      It was! It was brilliant. Honestly, Silly Stones might be the theme this time too.      No way! That sounds chaotic, but oddly fun.      I think the hotel has a games room. If we all make it in, there might be a Mario Kart tournament. Or a bad karaoke night. Either way, Sarah’s going to be absolutely loaded and not remember her own name by Friday.      Classic. I just hope her hangover doesn’t clash with her wedding vows on Saturday.      Oh, she mentioned the priest said he’d still marry her even if she walked down the aisle wearing a wig and declaring herself a Viking.      That’s the kind of woman we're talking about.      So, are you eating the chicken or am I eating it? It’s gone cold.      I was just admiring the artistry behind the burnt bits. You know what your chicken tastes like? It tastes like defeat and disappointment.      Fair enough, I’ll take your leftovers to fuel my revenge on the flight booking system.      I’m just going to watch Netflix to avoid going into debt.      Have you seen the new series everyone’s talking about?

Rather annoying this, isn't it, the whole phone lot. My number was working fine until they said they’d got to port it over to the new lot. Blows me how something like a phone contract ends up being a full-time job.      It is, honestly. Even if they live with someone else, the cost of running the place is too much.      Then again, if you can’t afford to go out much on your own, you end up losing so much of what makes life tick—like that nice bench we go to in the park when the weather’s nice.

Okay, so we've got this living room full of six people and we've got no idea what to order in. Has anyone thought about what they actually like yet?      I dunno, probably anything with cheese. Eventually, he learns that paper is not sentient and just gets sad because he’s out of practice chasing invisible squirrels.

So did you finish that art essay yet?      Not even close. I kept thinking I had heaps of time, but it’s like,  poof —all gone.      I feel you. Alright, let’s get back to mine. Just make sure to be nice when you read it.      I’ll be brutally honest but with a glitter pen on the margins. Deal?      Done. You know, you can say it was in writing on the first day, but they still think they can just treat you like their personal therapist. Oh it’s not the coursework I mind as much, but I had to go over to the faculty office yesterday and the fire alarm went off. Again. And that’s the third time this term! The head of department is like, “Oh, someone must’ve cooked pasta too close to the wall socket.” Sounds like they’ve got more problems than breakfasts. And then I walked past the house last week—John’s been trying to fix the kitchen sink, you remember? I told him a tradesperson would be cheaper in the long run. He’d listen to you, I’m sure. But as it is, now the hob’s making a funny noise. I mean, what if we’re in the middle of cooking Christmas dinner and the whole thing goes up in smoke? You said that last week and the week before. You’re already planning the first of December. Are we officially the only couple who worries about their gas hob at this point? You’d be surprised how many people are. I was in the grocery store the other day and overheard a woman next to me saying she hadn’t looked at her bill in about five days. That’s not worrying— that’s  alarming. I don’t even want to talk about the emails I get. The other day, I got a text at two in the morning from a guest speaker expressing concern that they hadn’t received their hotel booking confirmation. It was for next week! I’ve told them, I’ve told the chair, I’ve told the guest. And yet here we are, back in the same cycle next term. Some people just…  can’t . I sometimes think we should go back to the pond life if this keeps up.

So did you manage to sort out that weekend trip with your mates then?      Yeah, got the tent sorted out from Dad’s shed, and I’ve asked Tom to bring his tent as well. Should be okay. You know, I kind of miss our grandparents’ garden when it was all set up like that, with the big trampoline and stuff.      Yeah, I remember that. It always felt like summer in there, even in November. They used to keep it so well. You know, I was just sorting through some old photos the other day and it made me think... like, how did they make everything look so effortlessly nice? Even the furniture, you know? It wasn’t posh, but it felt homey.      Probably because they had the time, right? I mean I think modern life is just so chaotic everyone just settles for mass-produced stuff. I see all these urban farming initiatives now, like people trying to grow food on rooftops and in tiny gardens, which is pretty cool. But I still think there’s something missing—something practical and personal, maybe?      I think that’s a big part of what we’re missing, especially as we get more into automation and robots doing everything. I was reading the other day about how some schools are talking about careers advice, and now it's all about coding and AI and whatnot. But did they ever teach you about basic skills—like cooking, for example? Because from what I’ve seen at your age, a lot of young people just order in or microwave something.      Fair point. I can boil an egg, but otherwise I’m not much of a chef. Though I did make a bit of a mess of trying to cook the other night. It was meant to be easy stir-fry, but I scorched the pan and it all kind of fell to pieces. But honestly, I think the biggest problem is food wastage. Parents were better at using everything. I remember your mum was always saving the last bit of soup for tomorrow or using peelings to make something else.      Exactly. And with that plastic bag charge now, people have to think about it more. Still, I think a lot of it comes down to the education system. They need to teach about sustainability alongside all the techy stuff. I remember in my day, it was always the ‘traditional’ topics—maybe your generation is better off with more focus on modern issues?

Rather annoying isn’t it, how even simple things like turning on the oven can turn into such a routine. I got the kids to help me program the timer last week and they asked, “Is this a test?” I said, “No love, this is just being grown up.”      I find the more passive the weekend the more twitchy I feel if something isn’t scheduled. Like, I clean the coffee machine, but I still feel as if I’ve squandered the morning. It’s as if you have to justify the time.      I agree with you there. I like to think of weekends as  managed breaks . I do plan the odd supply list or review some journals now and then, but I also bake too much and left the house this morning with a half-eaten sandwich in my coat pocket and I hadn’t even screamed. Living with rules again is harder than working with them.      That’s true. I used to live on the idea of structure being anxiety, you know, always forcing flexibility, but once I became directly responsible for managing over 800 pupils’ progress, I quickly learned that if you don’t plan to be flexible, you’ll be too rigid to fix anything when it breaks—and it always breaks.      Ha – very good point. I deal with a similar kind of structure in my role. Conducting assessments in mental health settings, you have to know what to expect and what not to expect, and then also what someone  shouldn’t  expect. That balance is a daily struggle.      Just the other day a parent phoned and asked me if their child’s  discomfort coping level  was a score out of 10. I had to politely explain that it’s not a scoring system—it’s more like a barometer that you check regularly and it changes depending on the day and the task.      That’s something I notice about working in health: you often become the translator for something technical into something human. I tried to do that when I gave a lecture on psychosocial factors in rural communities. I mentioned how stigma affects people’s treatment engagement and one student asked if I meant going to church too much. I had to say, gently, no—that it's more complicated than that.      But it makes you question how much of that gap is down to background differences or societal divides.

Rather skip the newfit and go through the request, ain't I?      Oh, come on, James, you're not serious. Blows all your cover.      Covers? Not like I’ve seen one in years!      Both of yeh are being  ridiculous . You can’t just sit on the doorstep all day like a wet paperbag. Somebody’s gonna call the old bat and ring up the charity shop.      Well, you tell me, Paul. What else do I do? Sit in front of the telly, staring at some dodgy made-for-TV drama, and the only excitement I get is when the cat knocks the turkey pot off the side?      Tenpence to hear the cat knock something off the side today. Fair enough? But if you're stuck at home, forget the waiting room, just get involved. I mean, volunteer or something. I hear the church runs a lunch club every Friday, even if it is the same six people sitting there repeating the same stories over and over.      Yeah, I volunteered with the WI one summer. Did grief. Handed out jam sandwiches and read poetry to old ladies. Never seen a woman laugh so much at the word  ephemeral .      That’s not for me. I’d rather read the dictionary out loud and have tea with the cat.      There’s also this group at the community centre—feeding the birds, clearing the paths, gardening. Not a patch on floring the lawns mind, but it’s being outside. Can’t beat birdsong in the morning, eh? I mean, seeing those baby blue tits trying to leave the nest, chaotic little things they are.      Blue tits? I only handle the ungrateful lot that walk on two legs.      There's that. Come on, Val. Don't give up. I know money’s tight, I know your Arthritis is a pain, but you can't just fold up and stay in bed with your thoughts. That’s what got the old chap next door. Six months and a half a brain by the window, watching the curtains go by. You don’t want that.      I just feel, I don’t know— depressed , sometimes.      It’s normal, Val. You live long enough, you see those days creeping in. But don’t let ’em take you prisoner. Go out, meet people, do something. I tell you, my missus used to say: "The only cure for the blues is the red bus."

So did you go into Boots last week?      Yeah, I did. The first thing I did when I got home after the weekend. I picked up a few things after seeing that post on Instagram—y'know, those before and after brows?      Oh yeah, I saw that too. I’m seriously sorely tempted to invest in some of that wax they were showing. I don’t know if I’ve got this shape or that shape, but I’m clearly not pulling off "natural" at the moment.      Honestly, the worst thing isn’t the shape—it’s the split ends. I’ve been meaning to get my hair done for ages. It looks like I’ve been dragging it through a hedge backwards!      I’m with you there, love, but I’ve been saving up for a thermal style treatment for my nails. They’re so breakfast, no matter what I do. I tried this gel polish once at the salon, and it lasted weeks without chipping.      That does sound good—especially over Christmas when you get all the festive gloves and everything. I never thought about gel nail polish before, but I’m deadly with manicures. I did try acrylics once and it was a disaster. Ended up booking in for a remover session before the week was out!      Oh my God, don’t get me started. I once accidentally removed all my cuticles with that orangey cream. Looked like I had been attacked by a grudge-holding cat.      Okay, now that is a horrific image and I don’t need it at all. I did ballet as a kid and I did  not  walk away unscathed from those toe nails. I had ingrowns for years and I refused to take them off!      Maybe we’re just cursed, huh? Beauty and I have always had an adversarial relationship. The only thing I can do without crying is probably foundation. I once used Foundation 12 on my face by accident instead of my actual foundation and I ended up doing a Monica Geller with the concealer and paper towel!      Oh for God’s sake! You are truly a tragic icon of DIY goings-on. But seriously, maybe we should just go to that new esthetician in town that everyone’s raving about? Time to invest in your face and your hands at the same time?      I’m down! I’ll even take your discount voucher you got from your cousin—a gift that keeps on giving, right?

So did you go up to the World Museum last week? I was promising me mam I would take 'er when we was in Liverpool for Christmas. Otherwise she’d have been knocking on me door every day about it.      No, I didn’t get a chance. But it was snowing on Tuesday and my mam wanted me to take ‘er to see the Santa display in the town centre. I said yeah, but by the time I got outta work, there was a massive tailback in Mount Pleasant road. You can't park for love nor money up there when it's the school holidays.      Oh yeah, I remember that. Me and my girlfriend tried to go to the dock museum like that one Saturday, and I had to leave the car in a different ward altogether, half way up Woodside. But anyway, I reckon the museum is worth it if she likes that kinda thing. The upstairs breakfasts are good if you want a coffee after.      I know the museum's good, but to be honest, the town centre isn’t my favourite spot—especially when it’s crowded and Christmas is on. My sister got engaged two weeks ago, though. You didn’t tell me, did you?      No, really? Well then congrats to her. Who’s the lucky geezer?      Someone from her workplace. They’ve been seeing each other for like seven months now. She’s all ‘wedding planning’ and ‘getting the perfect ring’. Honestly, I said I’m not getting involved in the colour schemes or the cake. That’s above my pay grade.      Fair ‘nough. I had to help me cousin pick out a venue last year. Turns out the gold-leaf thing wasn’t a taste thing, it was just lack of funds. They had to dip and they didn’t tell the caterer in time. My aunt ‘ad a proper go at them for weeks.      Classic. I don’t think I’d survive all that. At least someone else is stressing out about that. So while you’re looking after your mam this Christmas, what about you? Family back up in Wirral?      Me parents are coming in for a few nights. I told 'em to go ahead of me and settle in the flat first. Just got it redecorated before anyone came, so I could go up last and see if the builders didn’t leave anything behind.

So do you not find it difficult?      Not really why would it be?      Just with being home all the time more or less, not having someone to talk to about stuff, or… you know, not feeling like you're contributing in the same way?      I mean, I used to think that, but I reckon it depends on your self-esteem, really. I don’t feel less because I’m not working, not like I used to. It takes time, that’s all.      Yeah, I suppose, but still… being a step-parent is tricky too, isn’t it? I mean, with your children, and then Rob’s, and trying to keep things light, not push too hard, not step on toes?      You're telling me. Rob said joking the other day that if he’d known about the step part he might have called a halt then and there.      Oh don’t I know it. There’s been some awkward family events. One time the daughter refused to speak to me for over a week because I told her she couldn’t take three tubs of ice cream as a bedtime snack.      Oh no! I can imagine how that went over. Be fair, Rob is relentless—he just gives it to her. He didn’t mind that one.      Doesn’t make me feel any better when Sil’s on the warpath.      There’s also this funny side to it. I mean, trying to be a good step-mum, then one day you catch yourself thinking about them in the way you used to think about your own kids. That’s when you know you’ve made the jump.      Oh yes, I’ve had that. I remember when Charlie started calling me “Mummy” instead of “Mum” for some reason. My heart nearly flipped. I didn’t tell Rob—he passed out laughing when I mentioned it later.      That’s sweet. At least someone knows how to appreciate it. My kids are my own, and I know what they’re like, but with Rob’s girls, it’s been more like trying to play mediator sometimes.      Mm. I think the thing I struggle with the most is if I ever feel… like I have less independence? I don’t see myself as less of a person or something, but your life kind of gets ordered around the children.      That’s exactly it. And I had friends, before, who expected me to have ‘me time’ every weekend, and now I’m like—‘me time’ is five minutes between nappies and tea.

So did you watch The Crown last night? That episode where they talk about the Suez Crisis?      No, I’ve been buried in my PhD readings. I've barely had time to blink, let alone watch proper telly. I heard it was a bit controversial though — was it that one where the timeline doesn't line up with the 'real' history again?      Aye, it’s starting to get that  spot-on, but not quite  vibe now. Still, it’s better than nothing, innit? Keeps me entertained when I don’t wanna watch  Love Island  again.      I get that. What I don’t get is how someone like you, who still lives with your mam, is left with a life of dramatic documentaries and crown intrigue.      Oh, shut your face! It's not about where I live! It's about priorities. You need to get out more, doc. And by more, I mean not in hides, you know, out. Out in the real world, meeting girls—      Oh, here we go. I can feel the rant coming.      What? I’m just saying… You live with five other blokes, all got Tinder profiles from 2014 with the same profile pic, and you expect to meet someone online? You need to diversify your dating pool!      Fine! Next weekend, I’m going out.      And not to some lecture or museum gig, mind. You need hotter places—maybe a bar or something. Maybe here, even!      Oy, I did meet someone last week! Online! Her name was Hannah. She liked my vibes.      Oh that was you! I met her sister at Charlotte’s birthday! Jokes, jokes! You need to stop being so high and mighty about your Tinder conquests.      Oh, I see. You meet girls, I meet girls, but who finishes the first round and manages to propose to them within three weeks?      Ah, right, the recent…  hubby  of mine. Picked him up in a bar in Middlesbrough, if you must know.      Wait, no, I genuinely didn’t know you two met through what your mam would call 'a proper meeting'.      Oh, she’d say that. Anyway, enough about me love life—what about you? You asked me about TV, so what about you—got something new on your watchlist?      Actually, I’ve been casting my eye over serial killer docos again. There’s one about Ted Bundy coming up before Christmas.      Oh, you stay away from that lot for a while.

Rather skip the newfitting eh?      Aye, just glim they’re like... What was it, five pounds?      Not even, like two quid! You’re mad. £2 for a bulb? We’ve got seven sconces in here. That’s £14, and we’ve got four more spots on the ceiling.      I said that only because I thought they’d be too showy, but now I’m checking the LED ones—actually, some of these are decent. You get the shaped ones, the ones with a glass cover... like, decent enough for a hallway.      What’s the point in buying cheap lights if you’re gonna look at them every day? I saw a fitting this morning on eBay, proper curved brass, with these little etched features—fiver. It looked like it could’ve come from a 1920s cinema!      Aye, and I’m no object to that, but then we’d be retrofitting the whole lot, and that’s time and effort.      Well, if I’m in the land of “I might as well,” then let’s talk property. I was on Rightmove last night, scrolling, and I swear half the houses look like they were built in 1930 and then forgot to be renovated.      Aye, I saw one with “character features” as an asset, and the description just said “charming lumps in the plaster.” That wasn’t inspiring.      And the ones that are new builds—eh, they look clean but feel... hollow. Like, there’s not a soul in them. No charm. I’m not interested in blinking white boxes with steel kitchens.      I agree, but I also don’t fancy a Victorian sprawl that’s just a time bomb waiting to flood. There’s got to be a balance somewhere.      Maybe a mid-century one? Like, 70s or 80s? Not too grand, not too derelict. Somewhere we can slap on a new coat of paint and call it home. I saw one near us—loft style, two up, two down. Looked like it had had a lick of renovation done.      Right, and it probably had the box rooms converted into a whatnot. Cos you know how it is—people think conservation and then add a dining kitchen that takes up half the house.      I know! And I mean, I’m not against modern conveniences—got my faults like anyone. But there’s a difference between being practical and being boring.

So did you talk to the manager about the request yet, Sarah?      Yeah, first thing this morning. I had no luck, I'm afraid. He said their shift cover is still a mess, and they can't do anything about extra time until things stabilize.      That’s a bummer. I understand the job’s tricky enough without extra shifts. But isn't that a bit of a slap in the face? I mean, you've been there for over a year now, pulling reasonable hours and always turning up on time. You deserve a bit of recognition or at least some flexibility.      I couldn’t agree more. That’s the problem with some of these setups — the system feels more like a grind than actual work. I left nursing a few years back, to be honest, because of the push and pull of hours and little thanks. It wore me out.      I know what you mean. It’s not just the hours — it’s the thanks, or lack of it, even when you go the extra mile. I remember one bloke I worked with, Bob, had PD and couldn’t really stand for long — no one would’ve asked, and I took on double the time just to make sure he didn’t have to rush. No one said a word at the time. Years later, I saw his daughter at the local shop, and she knew her dad had gone to the next life. She was so grateful toward me. That meant the world.      Oh no, that’s such a tough situation. It just goes to show how much what you do actually matters. It shouldn’t be taken for granted. That’s one thing about my job — it feels a bit more personal. I work with kids, the ones who’ve had chaotic upbringings — you see them grow, you see the small improvements. It makes it all worth while.      That must be so rewarding. I hear you’re looking after that new baby in the Simpson family now?      Yeah, that’s them. The poor thing’s only 11 months and already fighting off cold after cold. Mum’s at her wits’ end balancing the shop and the toddler. I tell her, "Just take a day if you need to — go out of the shop for an hour or two. You won’t go broke." But, no, she thinks she’s got to stay on top of everything all the time.

So did you read that article last night about sleep and how napping can actually improve your mood if done right?      Yes, I did. I think it said something about where you nap and for how long. You can’t just crash for an hour and expect to be refreshed, can you?      Exactly. They mentioned that if you sleep for about twenty to thirty minutes, you avoid the deep sleep cycles and wake up more alert. But if you stretch it into an hour or more, you’re basically grinding through the stages and dragging yourself out when your body wants to go deeper. I like to call it the  coffee tax —nap too long and you pay the price.      Ha, I like that. I think I’m guilty of over-napping now I’m home on these long weekends. The kids are off school for half-term, aren’t they?      Yeah, I noticed. They’ve taken to setting up a tent in the living room every morning, even though it's still light. One time, I thought I was dreaming when I walked into the kitchen and Lucy was proudly declaring that Wellington was calling a storm to wash away human dirt forever.      Sounds like fun. But it does remind me of when we camped in the South Island with your parents last summer. I still don’t know why the tent collapsed on our way to check the fire at 2 am.      Because you forgot to stake it down in one of the corners. That was me, by the way. I definitely said out loud something like, “Of course the bit of ground here is a bit hilly.”      I still remember Steve trying to fly off the ridge without the tent poles. It was like a cross between  Lord of the Rings  and  The Muppets .      But honestly, the beauty of New Zealand’s highlands at night was exceptional. I remember looking up at the stars and thinking,  this is it—the way you should be living forever.  We should go back as soon as we can. Even if it’s just for a weekend campout with the kids.      I’d love that. Though next time, maybe we can go in a group? If I get lost again, or worse, find my way into a farmer’s paddock with the boxy tent on my back, I’m not sure I have the fluency to explain to a New Zealander that I really don’t want to be a third farm dog.

So did I! The way he ran off with the bedding scattered everywhere—it was like a hamster apocalypse. I got to pick it all up after, like,  my  personal gym session      Honestly, I can't even imagine dealing with a frightened hamster. Mine just lie there looking at me like,  'Whatever'       Yeah, I had one of those once—just stared at me. Not scared, not curious, just... indifferent. I started to get a bit offended.      Oh yeah? Well when mine ran off with a piece of my cheese, I had to go  sniffing around  the room like a dog. Honestly, I’m never giving him a doorstep again.      Doorstep? I didn’t know they had them!      Oh they do, in the fancy ones. Probably better for breakfast, though—maybe he’d just go for a bit of nut and a sip of non-dairy milk, you know?      That would be ideal—viral moment, anyone? 'Here’s a hamster enjoying smoothie with brunch.'      Haha, only if there was a hashtag for it. #HammieWithTheJuice.      I feel like gingers take the cake when it comes to pet names though. All these ridiculous nicknames.      True! I had a classmate in Year 11 called Ginger who got given the nickname Hairflame just for looking sour at an email.      I worked in a shop once with a Ginger barista who looked like he hadn't slept in days. We just called him “Baked Salmon”      That's not even a little bit cruel. That's national treasure cruel.      Yeah, but fair. If he looked like that and had ginger hair, I’d probably be the one giving him the nickname too.      Honestly, I sort of admire the creativity. Like, I know of one called "-ish." Because 'hey mate, ginger—you're  reddish !'      Classic. Pisses people off heaps but it's so common it's funny if you don’t get it.      It’s brutal. I had a bloke in college who had to change his nickname at the start of the year. Thought it was cute to go for “Ginge,” then someone else already had it. He changed to “Reed’s Revenge,” which nobody thought was fun.      Always forget there are people who think red hair names are always a good idea.      It’s not all flippin’ and slapstick. A few of my cousins actually enjoy it—loads of inside jokes, and stuff. Makes for a pretty tight group if you've got red-haired family.

Right Aaron’s taking New York again. You can’t just do that every time. Someone’s got to stop him or the game’ll be over in ten more moves. I’ve had it up to here with his “I’m cashing in my continents” nonsense.      Look, if it’s all the same to you, I’m just going to enjoy the wine and not get involved in this. I’ve only played this once before and that was back in ’92 with my old mates in Liverpool. We drank three bottles and ended up invading each other’s houses in the real world. Tore the kitchen apart, I tell you! Not because I was mad, no. Just because no one had a card for Australia.      Aaron though… I’m not sure he knows the difference between Geneva and Geneva, Illinois anymore. The map turned into a mess an hour ago. Someone should’ve patched it when it started slipping off the wall. Brian here tried to reattach it with tape, and looked like he was putting plaster on a dead animal.      I mean I do like the way we’ve gone back to the 1995 rule set. No AI deciding when continents get re-shaped. Good old fashioned country borders, proper armies, and then of course… the most important – no digital updates, no sneaky version 2.3 patches changing the rules mid-game. It’s just you and the board.      Still, if we carry on like this someone’s going to end up with a headache from arguing over the pronunciation of  Phnom Penh  and the kid’s gonna have to call the police again. That was a  disaster . Poor Aaron had to do five laps of the garden trying to explain the game wasn’t real.      Oh speaking of young people, you remember Suzy? The one who moved out to do her dance course? Turns out she ended up pregnant after meeting some guy called Aaron. He vanished by the time they told us. Do you know how disappointed her grandparents are? Her grandmother still sends me these Chinese herbal teas and says they "nourish the spirit".      Ah the old Chinese medicine. My grandad used to swear by this tincture he called "dragon goop". I think it was just antiseptic or something, but he insisted it cured malaria, cancer and loneliness in three goes.      Look mate, I’ve made it to the conference stage twice in my life.

So do you really think we’ve made the right choice, like, uni and all this? ‘Cause like... I don’t know, I’m just having one of  those  days today      Aww don’t do that, I mean—      —proper day een? I mean, I used to think I wanted to study creative writing or something all artsy, but now I’m like, “What the hell am I doing here?”      You’re gonna be a world-famous author. You write the best gob, don’t even try to tell me otherwise.      Aww, thanks, but real talk—employers don’t like that sort of thing. You’ve met enough interns to know no one gets jobs from just writing essays about D.H. Lawrence and sad twats.      They do eventually giggle. I mean—look at Lena Dunham. What d’you want outta all this? Lecturing in boring business stuff to a room of dead-eyed students or something?      Or I could get a job at L’Oréal and come up with make-up lines about how even Steve McQueen would be jealous of my eyeliner       Wait—that fails at “how to plug gaps in self esteem” unival       Okay, fair. Do lunches with a new A-lister every week       Unless something amazing comes up like a man with lots of goon money on the internet, you end up doing extra at the Proms line in the Catherine Tate Show.      Aww your face was like a sumo about to faint      I was hours away from fainting belly-laugh to myself.      Look, we’re all gonna be 30 in like two weeks, so if we don’t sort it now, we might end up like Kim C but with very little make-up      A) Kim C before 30 is pinnacle, B) I don’t want my last words to ever be, “Mum, am I a failure yet?”      Exactly.

So do you think we actually need to do that part about calculating the median income for the project?      I don't know, mate. But I heard from someone that the teacher said we should include it. Yeah, but if you’re rich and you’re smart, you can still be poor in a way, can't you? Like being poor in connections or something?      Yeah, that makes sense. I’ve got my three-year-old and a toddler, and it’s like trying to run a circus half the time. Speaking of which, how’s the new dog getting on? I remember you said you were thinking about getting a second one.      Oh yes, well Mylo, the golden retriever, is brilliant. And we just got a little Shih Tzu from the rescue centre I volunteer at. Her name’s Lila, and she’s absolutely adorable. I brought her home last week, and everyone goes mad for her — even my teenagers, which is surprising!      Oh, that’s lovely. I’d love to get a rescue, but between work and the kids, I don’t think I’ve got the energy. I only started back at the language school properly a couple of months ago.      Oh, how’s that going? Still teaching Spanish, I hope?      Yeah, but I’m actually making a bit of a change. I’m doing some courses now — like online business Spanish. Who’d have thought it? I’ve got a few clients who work in the textiles industry, so it’s all about developing a specialist niche. It’s exciting, but I’ve had to learn a few new words I hadn’t even heard of before!      Oh, well I’m not surprised. My son is starting an apprenticeship in the logistics industry, and believe it or not, he found out that quite a few of the clients are Spanish-speaking. He ended up at me asking for help with a few basic phrases!      That’s brilliant! You must be really proud as a mum. Let’s see... What else? Family apart from the kids and the dogs?      Well, I’ve had a bit of a mishap with my hair lately. I tried this new smoothing treatment, and I think I might have gone a little too far. My hair was all over the place, and after one application, I looked like I’d been struck by lightning.

So do you lot actually know what you're meant to be doing for the Seder tonight, or is it just me and my aunt yelling out instructions every five minutes?      Oh, we watched that YouTube video… with the guy in the kippah making matzo ball soup while singing in Hebrew. That counted as  reading the Haggadah , right?      You don’t need to be a  good  singer, just human. The important thing is telling the story, not belting out a tune nobody knows the words to. Didn’t your mum get the guide I sent her?      I  promised  I’d bring the Seder plate, but I have no idea what’s on it. I’m still double-checking if this bottle of wine is kosher for Passover. I feel like I’m taking the SAT of Jewish traditions in one night.      I made the charoset! My interpretation is apple, nutella, ginger, and a bit of feta to give it that Middle Eastern twist. It’s  Italian  charoset.      Oh, Italy. I went with my uncle last summer and had this amazing Passover meal in Rome. Real Italian Jewish food—way lighter than what we get here. They use more olive oil instead of butter. I almost cried, it was so good.      It’s amazing how Jewish food changes from place to place, isn’t it? Like, in New York, someone I met called brisket the “King of Shabbat,” and I had no idea what they were talking about.      I’m just curious if all the biblical references are in there for a reason. Why do we remember the ten plagues in the order we do? I thought it was more of a themed storytelling thing.      Dude, we went to that museum last week. Pharaoh died first, waters turned to blood, frogs came out of nowhere… yeah, it’s a timeline. Do  not  mess with the order or your grandmother will excommunicate you from her  menorah of pride .      I’ve tried to learn a few words of Hebrew, you know, for saying blessings and stuff. But it’s hard. My phone doesn’t let me text in Hebrew unless I download some dodgy app. Imagine baking a challah and spelling ‘blessed’ backwards due to right-to-left script. I might seriously kill someone.      And speaking of baking… I gave your aunt a list of what to bring over—matzo, wine, bitter herbs… and  maror , I think that's the same?

Rather skip the new season of  The Great British Bake Off  then – I hear it’s back in front of a live audience, but honestly, I’m more interested in our book club pick. Did we manage to get a consensus on reading  The Night Fire ?      Aye, it’s all booked out at the library. I was lucky enough to get one of the last copies. Though I’ve been neglecting it with all the admin this month. Still, easier said than done to put a book down when it’s been queued up for weeks!      Oh, I pre-ordered the audiobook! Still haven’t made time to listen, though. I’ve only got through two chapters so far. Honestly, I’m living in a bit of a book-free zone – I’m knitting like crazy, trying to pick up the skills before the grandkids come over in October.      I envy you that. I’ve been wanting to try crocheting a scarf, but the yarn I bought got tangled in the spare room so badly that I gave up and just painted over it with a big canvas of inappropriate emojis. My husband laughed himself silly, honestly.      It’s not like you to go for something so… fun. Normally it’s all spreadsheets and forecasts. Ha – but I get it. Sometimes, you just need to  not  be the one managing the accounts for once.      Speaking of which – Ruth, your sister, rang me earlier this week. Spent half the call crying because my nephew insists e-readers are 'boring' and won’t let him read a physical copy of  Harry Potter . I said  literally every generation has said that about the last . Seems he's not quite the Renaissance lit major he claimed to be.      Tell me about it. My daughter treats paper books like they’re going to crumble at her touch. I showed her my well-thumbed copy of  Jane Eyre  from the 80s and all she said was, “Can you just read it on your iPad while you fold laundry?”      Ah, Gen Z. We keep preaching “books are the future” and next thing you know, they’re saying ‘volumes are the past’.      But let’s not talk about them – what about the rest of us? I’m dying to know – did either of you catch the new season of  Bridgerton ? I watched the first three episodes and am now wondering if I’ll regret not watching it more than I already have.

Right, I just got my shiny new phone off the parcel. Blimey, it’s like unboxing a gift and I’m mid-40s, not a teenager. But this one’s gotta be better than that Nokia brick we had 15 years back!      Yeah, I saw the new Nokia ad on the telly and thought, “Oh no, they’re not going back retro are they? I still have the one from 2002!”      Oh, and you remember the one where you could drop it in the wash and it’d still work? That was a holy grail of durability. Still, technology’s moved on, and these new ones have like apps for everything, even changing your phone settings!      I’m terrified I’m gonna break it, and I’m sitting in Finland of all places – the old home of Nokia!      Look, while you're here for your placement at the uni, maybe I can show you some tricks. I’ve been using the Oneplus since forever, so I should know a few shortcuts for setting it up.      You’re assuming I didn’t already set mine up as soon as it got here. I tried installing it in Finnish and got so confused.      Oh, you speak Finnish now?      No, don’t be daft. Silly program didn’t let me switch back to English, and then there was someone at the phone shop who suspiciously looked like me and tried to give me a tablet instead.      Typical. I swear these phone shops still think all tourists are in the Prime of their Apple Years. I’m lucky I speak German a bit – the Finnish lot were friendly but didn’t understand my accent!      I’m jealous. I could probably cope if the system wasn’t so weird.      Let’s face it, at least they don’t have a landline network anymore. We don’t need them for waiting half an hour while the bell rings and then speakerphone being 99% static with your gran shouting on the other line. Now it’s all instant, just faster, even around this tannoy pub.      But it’s more complicated too. Just today I had my voicemail, password, SMS settings all in three different places on the same app.      I’ll help you sort it out after I’ve taught you how to lock your photos properly. I had someone in my lecture over this – said they lost them all because they didn’t have my cunning settings tips.

Mummy, I've been thinking about our birthday party for Lucas. I was wondering if we can get like... real Red Pandas to come?      Oh, sweetheart, we can't exactly borrow real Red Pandas. They live in the wild and in zoos. But maybe we can draw one, or we can get a panda print for the decorations?      Yeah, but a paper one is not the same! I mean, I saw a YouTube video where someone made a cardboard Red Panda that moved! Maybe we could do something like that?      That sounds amazing. If we can get enough helpers, we could make a moving puppet panda to surprise Lucas when he opens presents. What do you think, Ollie?      [gurgling, then babbling in Irish] "Bláth, bláth!"  [flower, flower]       Maybe we could include Malamooche in the party too. Lucas’s cat is so tiny, and Malamooche is so big and fluffy. They’d be like best friends.      I hope Lucas doesn’t mind if we bring Malamooche. Do you think his parents will say yes?      [babbling then laughing] “Goo goo – Matey!”  [repeats, cheeps]       Yeah, maybe we ask when we go for the gymnastics lesson. Oh! And I saw a Japanese movie the other day that had pandas in it—Lucas would like it. It had animated pandas doing gymnastics—kinda like what we do in class.      A Japanese movie with ballet pandas? That does sound about right for boys your age. I can check it out when we go to the library.      Oh, and we could play some board games too! Maybe something like Jumanji but for little kids. Or maybe even use the iPad to play that animal memory game where you try to find the matching pictures.      I think your iPad is still in the charger. Why don’t you log in and see if you've got the game on there? I’ve got some tea going, and you can help me run through the guest list on the laptop if you want.      Cool! I can write down the schedule on the laptop too, so we know when the party will be.      Great! So far, it's scheduled for Saturday, after your gymnastics lesson, right?      Yeah! And if I get this one film on the iPad, Lucas can watch it while we all sit around eating cake. I was thinking of making red velvet cupcakes, like pandas!      Oh, that’s a sweet idea.

So do you lot actually do anything for Christmas at all, or do you just open a few tins and call it a day?      Blows! That's like negativity, Liv! We do proper stuff. We do loads, like, fairy lights, Christmas songs on repeat, mince pies—proper ones, not the American trifle-shaped ones.      Yeah? I reckon that sounds like proper working-class Christmas in this country, to be fair. Out here we get grandparents, turkey, and Auntie Jan doing the.Fatalfalls shuffle during the football.      Oh, I like it! In our day, we used to cut out paper snowflakes and have hot cocoa.      Ha! Yeah, and you’d throw in a little brandy if your parents thought no one was watching.
